articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: With other contenders making big trades, the Rams have to figure out a way to keep up
articles.summary: Given the Rams' history of aggression on the trade market, and how active they in the offseason, it's hard to believe they'll sit this trade deadline out.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams pushed a lot of chips to the middle of the table over the offseason. Then, when they came out of the gates slow, other teams saw an opportunity.

Last week, the Seattle Seahawks made a big move for guard Quenton Nelson and the San Francisco 49ers got a big acquisition in defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. The NFC West got a lot harder.

The Chicago Bears, clearly believing the NFC is up for grabs, traded a couple first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . His stellar play on Monday night in his Bears debut has lifted Chicago's ceiling for this season. Other top NFC teams will inevitably add to their rosters.

The Rams need to look to see if they have any more chips remaining to up their bet.

Head coach Sean McVay says the Rams aren't likely to be buyers. He says the team is content to have key players who have been on injured reserve, like defensive end Myles Garrett and wideout Davante Adams, provide the boost that a trade deadline acquisition normally would.

"The amount of guys that have not been available, that are key and focal points for really both sides of the football, you look at those guys hopefully being able to return within a month," McVay said, according to the Los Angeles Times , "and that's kind of where that value lies for us."'

Given the Rams' history, and how aggressive they were in the offseason leading up to this season, that's difficult to believe.

The Rams are already committed. They made huge trades for cornerback Trent McDuffie and Garrett, and also added a big signing with cornerback Jaylen Watson. They have already traded draft picks in the first, fifth and sixth rounds this year, in the first and third in 2027, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. There's no turning back now. And they're looking to make big deals at anytime, even in years they weren't big preseason Super Bowl favorites.

The Rams' 2-4 start was stunning. Garrett underwent knee surgery and there have been few updates on a timetable for his return. Then they suffered an injury to a position that was already perilously thin, when Adams injured his hamstring. He's out for six to 10 weeks, and there's no guarantee a player who turns 34 years old in December rebounds from an injury like that. The Rams can mask the injury with a lot of three tight end sets and running the ball more, but they won't be the same explosive offense from a season ago. The need at receiver beyond Puka Nacua is glaring.

The Rams are 4-4 after a couple straight wins, which keeps them in the NFC race, but their .500 record and the activity around the NFC West is a reminder that there's still a gap they need to close. Perhaps that occurs through the star players that will return from injury, though that's tough to depend on. Or maybe the Rams decide that now isn't the time to stop trading.

Panic meter: The Rams won't want to make all of the moves they made and then regret that they didn't make another one or two more.

The most likely answer for what happens next for the Baltimore Ravens is that they fade completely out of the playoff race and into a tense offseason with Lamar Jackson. The Ravens have been a bad team without Lamar Jackson, who is going on injured reserve with a thumb injury, and it is very likely that they'll be without Tyler Huntley for at least Week 9. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who is dealing with an ankle injury of his own, isn't keeping the team afloat, nor is newly signed QB Austin Reed.

The other truth is that it's practically impossible to pick up a quarterback who can save your season in November. Good starters are never available. Good backups are rarely available and you'll have to overpay for one. Bad starters and bad backups aren't fixing anything. The rare third option who can start, like Jacoby Brissett, might help for a little bit but we all know the outcome there. Over the past two seasons, before Sunday, Arizona was 3-16 in Brissett's starts.

When you lose a future Hall of Fame quarterback, there's no way to fix it.

Panic meter: The truth is the Ravens' season is done, barring a miracle.

If it wasn't for the Super Bowl bluster before the season, and the promises from owner Jerry Jones to make huge trades to chase a title , the obvious path for the 3-5 Cowboys might be to sell before the trade deadline. Nobody should think that Jones is going to do that.

The Cowboys were embarrassed yet again Sunday, blowing a 14-point lead and losing to the Cardinals. Even if people believe they can still win the NFC East, there are no signs they are good enough to be any factor in the playoffs. They haven't beaten a team all season that has more than two wins. The defense is impossibly bad. The offense hasn't been great either.

The Cowboys have no logical reason to believe that things will get much better. There's nobody available in the trade market who will fix everything, and giving up more future picks seems unwise for a bad team. But good luck convincing Jones of that.

Panic meter: The Cowboys are basically the NFL version of the "This is Fine" meme with the dog drinking his coffee surrounded by flames.

Jefferson left after the Vikings' loss to the Lions Sunday without speaking to the media. There was a message within that, even if Kevin O'Connell tried to smooth it over by saying Jefferson was a competitor and he wanted to win. That's probably part of the story.

Kyler Murray missed Jefferson on multiple throws . It has to feel like a repeat of last season, when Jefferson didn't have a quarterback who could get him the ball. Even though Murray has been an inconsistent player most of his career, the Vikings tabbed him to fix their quarterback issues. Now they have an offense that's struggling. The defense has carried the team to a 6-1 record. But it will be hard to maintain anywhere near that pace if the offense doesn't improve. It's not like the Vikings can change course at quarterback before the deadline (unless they completely overpay for Kirk Cousins, who the Raiders might not trade anyway and it wouldn't be smart regardless). It's just a team that has to win despite its imperfections.

Panic meter: Tensions are always high after a loss, but the underlying offensive issues are real.

When you start trading your best players, it's hard for the remaining players to stay motivated during a lost season. The Indianapolis Colts saw that up close on Sunday.

The Colts were putrid in a 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Had Jaguars coach Liam Coen held some grudge against Indianapolis, it seemed Jacksonville could have won by 60. There was no fight or pride in the Colts, especially without guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.

It won't get better. More trades are probably coming. Running back Jonathan Taylor, defensive tackle Grover Stewart and receiver Josh Downs could all be dealt. The only question left for coach Shane Steichen is if it gets so bad that the Colts have to fire him during the season rather than wait until it's done.

Panic meter: The Colts are 2-6 and a 2-15 finish seems realistic.

articles.title: “I might not be able to walk again”: Tyreek Hill’s potential Chiefs return faces another hurdle as concerns over his recovery continue
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has been out of the field for more than a year after he sustained severe injuries last September.
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has been out of the field for more than a year after he sustained severe injuries last September. The star wide receiver was later released by the Miami Dolphins. Amid this, Tyreek Hill has been dealing with rumors concerning a potential reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs. While things remain uncertain, Tyreek Hill’s comments about his injury have resurfaced.Tyreek Hill’s comments on his severe injuries resurface amid rumors of a potential reunion with the Kansas City ChiefsBack in July, the 32 year old star wide receiver Tyreek Hill weighed in on his severe injuries as he said, “So it’s about 10 months after doing two surgeries…My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg at all, so I’m trying to regain all the power back in my left leg.”The former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver added, “I’ve been activating the quads, the glutes, the hamstrings, the calves. I’ve been doing all the stability work, all the mobility work I need to get my knee back right. But it’s one day at a time…”Tyreek Hill continued, “You know, they told me I might not be able to walk again, and the doctor is like, ‘Bro, we don’t know what’s going to happen with your future,’ and now look at me. God is good,” Hill said.At this point in time, Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus has clarified that the star wide receiver is ready to get back to the field and has fully recovered from the multiple ligaments he tore in his left knee, including his ACL and LCL.Despite the constant reassurances, Tyreek Hill’s comeback to the field has sparked serious doubts if he has fully recovered.To make matters worse, the star wide receiver also recently travelled to Munich, Germany to seek specialised treatment for his injuries.This has sparked serious concern if Tyreek Hill is even fully ready to get back to the field with any team in the new season.Tyreek Hill’s legal trouble sparks concern about being suspended in the leagueWhile Tyreek Hill’s health remains a topic to debate about, there have also been serious concerns if he will be suspended even if he attempts to comeback to the field.For the unversed, Tyreek Hill was involved in serious legal trouble with his estranged wife accusing him of domestic violence.A Miami-Dade jury found Tyreek Hill liable on 2 of 10 domestic violence and battery counts, while clearing him of the remaining eight claims including severe emotional distress and continued domestic violence.The NFL has not confirmed if any action will be taken on Tyreek Hill as things remain uncertain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Grade the trade: Ravens get much-needed quarterback help with Jacoby Brissett
articles.summary: The Ravens found a starting quarterback after their top two QBs suffered injuries.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens had two quarterbacks suffer injuries Sunday that sent both to injured reserve. They had to do something just to get through the rest of the season.

At the same time the Ravens were in a nightmare at Buffalo on Sunday, the Arizona Cardinals benched their starting quarterback. Jacoby Brissett was taken out late in the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys and replaced by Gardner Minshew II. Minshew led a comeback win over the Cowboys, and the Cardinals announced that Brissett would be the third-string quarterback behind Minshew and rookie Carson Beck. Brissett seemed like an obvious candidate to get traded. The Ravens were an obvious candidate to trade for a quarterback.

On Wednesday, the most obvious swap possible happened when news broke from NFL Media that the Ravens were finalizing a trade for Brissett. That will reportedly be official over the weekend, which means the Ravens will have to start Joe Fagnano on Thursday night against the Jaguars. But at least the Ravens have a viable option for the rest of the season.

The truth of the NFL is teams don't want to trade their starting quarterbacks or their backup quarterbacks either. It's rare that a team has a third-string quarterback that can come in and start right way for another team.

The Ravens were never going to find a quarterback who can completely save their season, but Brissett will at least allow them to run a competent offense. Brissett was the Cardinals' starter for most of the past two seasons and threw for 5,085 yards with 33 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. That didn't lead to many wins for Arizona, but the Cardinals don't have a good supporting cast. The Ravens are in much better shape. And Brissett can at least get the ball to playmakers like Zay Flowers.

Nobody should believe Brissett will save Baltimore's season and help them win the division. The Ravens are 4-4 and will be starting undrafted rookie Fagnano against a good Jaguars team on Thursday. But Brissett was the best option available, and he at least makes sure the Ravens aren't playing out the string with uncompetitive football for two months. And maybe a miracle happens and the Ravens are still in contention by the time Jackson returns — if he can.

The Cardinals probably knew, when they made Brissett their third-string quarterback on Monday, that he wouldn't be with the team by the end of the week.

It's a perfectly reasonable move. The Cardinals are going to start Beck soon to get a look at him by next season. Minshew can do as well as Brissett in the short term. They presumably get to add a little bit of draft capital (terms weren't reported immediately) for a player who wasn't going to see the field the rest of the season and has an expiring contract. They also allow Brissett a chance to play meaningful football the rest of the season after serving as their starter for most of the past two seasons.

It's not an overly meaningful move for the franchise, but fine for the Cardinals for getting a deal done quickly.

articles.title: Donna Kelce put her own happiness on hold to give Jason and Travis Kelce a better life, but her story of a mother's sacrifice goes far beyond football
articles.summary: Long before Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce became Super Bowl champions and household names, their mother, Donna Kelce, was quietly making sacrifices that
articles.body: Long before Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce became Super Bowl champions and household names, their mother, Donna Kelce, was quietly making sacrifices that shaped their lives. She spent years balancing a demanding banking career, raising two boys with big sporting dreams and putting her family’s needs ahead of her own happiness. While the world now celebrates what her sons have achieved, Donna’s story is about everything she carried before they ever reached the NFL.What made Donna Kelce stay in an unhappy marriage for Jason and Travis Kelce?For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never just about taking her children to school, attending their football games or making sure they had everything they needed. It also meant making difficult personal decisions, even when those choices came at a cost to her own happiness.Donna and Ed Kelce were married for nearly 25 years. However, their relationship had reached a point where both knew things were no longer working. Rather than immediately ending their marriage, they decided to remain together while Jason and Travis were growing up. They wanted their sons to have as normal a childhood as possible, without having to deal with the difficulties that could come with their parents separating.Donna explained this decision during her October 2024 interview with Glamour for its Mothers of the Year feature. She said, “My husband and I knew that our marriage was not working, but we stayed together for the kids.”She also made it clear that their relationship was friendly, which helped them continue raising their children together. It was not a situation where the boys were left without support from either parent. Donna and Ed worked as a team, making sure their sons could focus on school, sports and their future.Ed also spoke about their decision in the 2023 documentary Kelce. He explained that separating earlier would have made it difficult to manage their sons’ schedules and provide the support they needed.For Donna, those years meant putting her personal life on hold. She did not hide how that affected her. During the same Glamour interview, she admitted, “But in that one respect, I did stand still for several years until I could move on on my own.”It is perhaps one of the most emotional parts of her story. She knew she wanted something different for herself, but she and Ed chose to wait until their sons had finished college and moved out before going their separate ways. Their marriage eventually ended, but their relationship as parents continued.How did Donna Kelce balance her banking career while raising two NFL stars?While raising Jason and Travis, Donna was also building a career of her own. She worked as a commercial banker across several states and steadily moved into senior positions. Her professional journey was not something she wanted to give up simply because she had children.In fact, she wanted her sons to grow up seeing that a woman could have a successful career, earn her own money and make important decisions for herself.Donna spoke about the effort she put into her work during her Glamour interview, saying, “I was a commercial banker for a bank in several different states. I wanted to get ahead. I worked really, really hard.”She was also a major breadwinner in the family, meaning that much of the financial responsibility rested on her shoulders. Between her job and her responsibilities at home, there was little room to put herself first.Jason later spoke about his mother’s career during his emotional retirement speech on March 4, 2024. He revealed that Donna had spent more than 40 years in banking, starting as a teller and eventually reaching the position of vice president.He also shared something about her childhood that helps explain where her determination came from. When Donna wanted to attend college, her father was against the idea. He believed she should become a secretary or a wife instead. However, Donna went ahead with her education and graduated from Ohio University.Her journey did not end there. She later earned an MBA from Baldwin Wallace University and continued working her way up in the banking industry.Jason said, “And from my mother, I learned the all too important lesson of never letting anyone tell you what you can’t do.”Those words carried a lot of meaning because he was not simply thanking his mother for supporting his football career. He was recognising the example she had set through her own life. Donna wanted Jason and Travis to understand that hard work and determination could take them further than anyone else’s expectations.Why did Jason Kelce’s retirement speech reveal so much about his mother?For years, Jason and Travis watched their mother manage work and family responsibilities, but children do not always understand how much their parents are doing behind the scenes. Jason admitted as much when he spoke about Donna during his retirement speech.As he looked back on his 13-year career with the Philadelphia Eagles, Jason made sure to recognise the people who had helped him reach that point. His mother received special attention, not only because she had supported his football journey but also because of the life she had built before he became a professional athlete.He spoke about how Donna had grown up in a time when many women were discouraged from pursuing higher education. Despite the advice she received from her father, she chose to attend college and build a career.Jason also recognised her financial contribution to the family, describing her as the person who was largely responsible for providing for them.For a mother who had spent so many years making sure her children had opportunities, hearing her son recognise those efforts on such an important day must have meant a great deal. His speech also showed that the lessons he had learned from Donna went beyond anything he could have picked up on a football field.He had seen her face challenges without allowing them to decide her future. He had watched her work hard, take responsibility and keep moving forward even when life was not easy.That is why his words about never allowing anyone to tell you what you cannot do were so important. They were not just a nice tribute to his mother. They were a reflection of the person Donna had been throughout his childhood.How did Donna Kelce’s sacrifices help shape the future of Jason and Travis Kelce?Donna’s story is also closely connected to the relationship Jason and Travis share. The brothers grew up playing sports together, competing against each other and supporting one another. Their parents made sure both boys had opportunities to follow their interests, even as their sporting ambitions grew.Jason eventually became one of the most respected centers in the NFL, spending 13 seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles before announcing his retirement in March 2024. Travis, meanwhile, built his career with the Kansas City Chiefs and became one of the league’s leading tight ends.Their success brought Donna into the public eye, especially when she became the centre of attention during Super Bowl LVII in February 2023. With Jason’s Eagles facing Travis’s Chiefs, she supported both sons by wearing a custom jersey featuring their names and team colors.But that famous moment was only a small part of a much longer journey.Donna had been there through their childhood games, college years, NFL dreams and difficult moments along the way. Jason even remembered in his retirement speech how he and Travis used to watch each other’s games, sitting with their mother and cheering for one another.He described their bond as something that had made him stronger throughout his life. Their childhood was filled with competition, laughter, arguments and shared dreams of becoming professional athletes.Donna and Ed helped give the brothers the support they needed to build those dreams. Even after their marriage ended, they continued to remain friends and support their sons.Donna’s life also shows that supporting children does not mean giving up every part of yourself. She continued to build her career, stood by her decisions and eventually made room for a new chapter in her own life.Today, people may recognise her as the mother of two NFL stars, but Jason’s retirement speech offered a much deeper picture of the woman behind that title. She was a working mother, a determined professional and someone who wanted her children to grow up knowing that their dreams were worth pursuing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson to practice Wednesday, while Rams CB Jaylen Watson will have season-ending surgery
articles.summary: Garrett logged his first practice session since going on IR after Week 1.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay provided injury updates for his team on Wednesday.

The updates were highlighted by both defensive end Myles Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson practicing in a limited capacity. McVay also told reporters that cornerback Jaylen Watson will have season-ending shoulder surgery.

Garrett has been sidelined since Week 2 with a knee injury that required arthroscopic surgery and landed him on injured reserve. The defensive end had to sit out a minimum of four games on IR, but he has missed the past seven games.

The injury's timing hurt even more for fans excited to see Garrett paired with the recently unretired Aaron Donald. As fate would have it, Donald wasn't ready to make his season debut until Week 2, so after Garrett was added to IR, Donald returned from 2.5 years of retirement.

Garrett and Donald could finally debut together this week against the Washington Commanders, depending on how Garrett's first week back at practice goes.

Ferguson has also been on injured reserve because of an ankle injury. He hasn't played since Week 3 and is one of several offensive skill-position injuries Los Angeles has been dealing with.

The Rams have a deep tight end room, but Ferguson caught seven passes for 63 yards and a touchdown before getting hurt.

While McVay announced two players are close to returning to game action, he also said the Rams will be without one player for the remainder of the season.

Watson will have season-ending shoulder surgery after getting multiple medical opinions. The cornerback has played in seven games this season and has 24 total tackles. He is one of only four Los Angeles players with an interception this season, logging his lone pick against the Buffalo Bills.

Los Angeles heads into this weekend's road game at Washington with a 4-4 record. The Rams entered the season as this year's Super Bowl favorite, but currently sit third in the NFC West.

articles.title: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen turned a $4.5 million land purchase into a $39.5 million mansion before listing it in 2019
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen once had an ambitious vision for a family home outside Boston.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen once had an ambitious vision for a family home outside Boston. What began as a multimillion-dollar purchase of vacant land eventually became one of the most talked-about celebrity properties in Massachusetts. The former couple invested $4.5 million in a sprawling Brookline plot in 2013 and built a custom mansion that attracted plenty of attention. Six years later, they put the finished estate on the market for $39.5 million, bringing their remarkable real estate journey into the spotlight.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen turned a $4.5 million land purchase into a luxury estateThe couple purchased more than five acres of land from Pine Manor College in 2013. Located in Brookline's Chestnut Hill area, the property offered privacy and an attractive setting alongside The Country Club golf course. Its location also placed the estate near the former home of New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft.Rather than settle for an existing property, Brady and Bündchen chose to create a home around their lifestyle. The result was a custom-built limestone mansion covering approximately 12,112 square feet.The residence offered far more than spacious bedrooms and impressive interiors. Its amenities included a private spa, a dedicated yoga studio, a wine cellar and a separate barn. For Bündchen, the barn held particular meaning. During a video tour of the property, she described it as her sanctuary, offering a glimpse into the quieter side of her life away from public attention.The estate also attracted viewers through Brady's documentary series, Tom vs. Time, and a separate home tour with Vogue in 2018. These appearances helped turn the private residence into a widely recognised celebrity property.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen listed their mansion for $39.5 millionIn August 2019, the former couple decided to test the luxury property market by listing their Brookline mansion for $39.5 million. The asking price was nearly nine times what they had paid for the land six years earlier. However, that comparison does not account for construction expenses, other investments or potential selling costs.The timing also drew attention because Brady was approaching the final season of his long career with the Patriots. His future in New England was already a major talking point, adding another layer of interest to the property listing.The asking price eventually dropped to $33.9 million in October 2019. Even with the reduction, the mansion struggled to attract a buyer. By May 2020, the property had been withdrawn from the market. The listing agent cited the coronavirus pandemic and its effect on luxury home sales. It later returned as an off-market listing.Brady's career, meanwhile, took a new direction. After spending 20 seasons with the Patriots, he joined the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020 and won another Super Bowl, securing his seventh championship ring.The Brookline mansion remains a notable chapter in the former couple's real estate history, combining an ambitious building project with a high-profile listing that never resulted in an immediate sale.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current helped 60 young women find their dream dresses through a special initiative
articles.summary: In 2024, the Kansas City Current turned a fashion event into an opportunity to make a lasting difference in the community.
articles.body: In 2024, the Kansas City Current turned a fashion event into an opportunity to make a lasting difference in the community. The NWSL club, co-owned by Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, teamed up with fashion rental company Nuuly and United Way of Greater Kansas City to donate nearly 100 designer dresses to local young women. The initiative gave 60 members of the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City a chance to find outfits for special occasions, while also creating an experience centred on confidence, self-expression and feeling valued.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current organised a special dress donation eventThe October 2, 2024, announcement revealed details of the club's collaboration, which brought fashion and community support together at the Boys & Girls Clubs' Thornberry Unit.The event, held on Tuesday evening, welcomed 60 middle and high school-aged girls. They could browse through nearly 100 donated designer dresses and choose outfits for homecoming or other important celebrations.The evening also featured a DJ, an interactive flower bar and a photo backdrop, making the experience feel more like a special shopping event than a traditional charity giveaway. Sparkling grape juice added another celebratory touch.Three KC Current players also joined the occasion. Defenders Hailie Mace and Gabrielle Robinson, along with forward Nichelle Prince, helped the girls explore different styles and select dresses they loved.Nuuly, which sponsors the club's Match Day Arrival, supplied the designer outfits. The subscription-based clothing rental service had more than 250,000 subscribers nationwide at the time.United Way of Greater Kansas City also played an important role by arranging tailors for on-site alterations. Dresses that remained after the event were kept at the Thornberry Unit so other club members could benefit from the collection.KC Current's partnership focused on confidence and community supportThe organisers wanted the evening to offer more than free clothing. For the young participants, choosing an outfit for an important occasion could help them feel comfortable expressing their personalities.“We’re thrilled to partner with the Kansas City Current, Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City and United Way of Greater Kansas City to help bring this memorable experience to life for these young women,” said Kim Gallagher, Nuuly Executive Director of Marketing and Customer Success. “At Nuuly, we believe in the power of clothing to inspire confidence and create special moments. It’s an honor to contribute to such a meaningful event.”Jason Roth, president and CEO of the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City, also highlighted the impact of the initiative.“This collaboration with the Kansas City Current, Nuuly, and United Way of Greater Kansas City means so much to the young women we serve,” said Jason Roth, president and CEO, Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City. “It’s about more than just receiving a dress – it’s about building self-esteem, encouraging self-expression, and creating unforgettable memories. We’re thankful to our partners for creating such a meaningful experience that uplifts and empowers our members.”For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, the initiative also reflected the Current's connection with Kansas City beyond the football and soccer fields. Their club's involvement showed how professional sports organisations can use their platforms and partnerships to create meaningful opportunities for local families.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL odds, betting, storylines: 2 underdogs to back in Week 9
articles.summary: Let's look at two spots where some 'dogs are in position to bark in Week 9.
articles.body:
If the NFL betting community handed out a first-half MVP award, there is no question who this year's runaway winner would be: big NFL underdogs.

Through eight weeks, seven teams have taken the field as double-digit underdogs. Five of them covered the spread.

So far, we have seen 37 underdogs of six points or more (including those seven double-digit pups). Their ATS record: 24-10-3 ATS.

This includes a 6-2 ATS mark posted by the largest underdog of the week. In fact, the biggest underdog has covered the spread each of the last five weeks and recorded three outright upsets.

All of which brings me to my trio of NFL underdog best bets for Week 9. Spoiler alert: I expect big 'dogs to continue barking.

After an uneven 2-2 start to the season — a start that included a frantic overtime home win against the Saints, blowout road losses to the Bills and Panthers, and zero covers — the Lions have turned things around.

The bounce-back began with a 45-21 thumping of the Cardinals in Arizona. Detroit then followed its bye with consecutive divisional home wins over Green Bay and Minnesota. Those wins, however, were hardly convincing. The Lions needed a last-second field goal to upend the Packers 20-17 and a late-game touchdown and defensive stop to hold off Minnesota 19-15.

So seven games into the 2026 season, Detroit has defeated just two opponents by more than four points: Arizona and the New York Jets (who lost 31-24 in Motown in Week 3). The Lions also enter Week 8 having covered only two point spreads.

Now they head to South Beach in what is a classic letdown/sandwich spot.

The letdown part: Detroit just barely beat two NFC North rivals in tense, down-to-the-wire games (both of which were at home). Now with their confidence sky high, the Lions hop on a plane to face one-win Miami.

The sandwich part: Detroit next week kicks off a three-game homestand against New England. So this is the team's only road trip over a six-game stretch.

My point is that this is a tricky situation for the Lions. Which means it's an advantageous one for the Dolphins, who have been much more competitive over the past month.

Since opening with double-digit losses to the Raiders, 49ers and Chiefs by the combined score of 86-36, Miami has upset the Jets 28-25 on the road and held its own against the Vikings (15-10 road loss as a 10-point underdog), Bengals (31-24 home loss as a 7-point underdog) and Patriots (24-19 home loss as a 7-point underdog).

Yep, Miami comes into this contest on a 3-0-1 ATS run. And while the defense has admittedly struggled most of the season, the offense has picked it up recently. Since tallying 13, 13, 10 and 10 points in their first four games, the Dolphins averaged 23.7 points in the last three.

If the offense can exceed that average Sunday by a tiny bit — against a Detroit defense that I'm not convinced is fixed — Miami will get inside this big number.

Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders

In Week 1, the Commanders traveled to Philadelphia as 6-point underdogs. They lost 24-22.

Two weeks later, with injured starting quarterback Jayden Daniels on the sidelines, the Commanders hosted defending champion Seattle as 8.5-point underdogs. They won 33-31.

Fast-forward to Week 6, and Washington traveled to San Francisco as a 7.5-point underdog on Monday Night Football. The 49ers won — but only by six points (23-17).

Those were the three biggest point spreads the Commanders have faced as an underdog this season. And they covered them all. Now they're catching a bunch of points against the visiting Rams, who have looked much better the last two weeks, thumping the Raiders and Chargers by the combined score of 59-30.

But let's not forget that this same Rams squad preceded those two wins with an 18-16 loss to Arizona as a 12.5-point home favorite. Before that, L.A. suffered an overtime home loss to Buffalo; needed a furious late fourth-quarter rally to win at Philadelphia; and blew a 16-0 halftime lead in a 30-26 loss at Denver.

Back to Washington: True, it got crushed 37-20 at Dallas as a 4.5-point underdog in Week 2. But it lost Daniels to an elbow injury right before halftime.

The Commanders also fell 30-13 to the Colts in London as 5-point underdogs in Week 4. But seventh-round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis played the majority of that game after backup Marcus Mariota went down early.

Daniels finally returned the following week, which was the now-infamous 27-27 tie against the Giants (who are 4-2-1). Then came the competitive loss at then-unbeaten San Francisco, followed by an off week, followed by last Sunday's 27-10 rout of the Eagles.

Bottom line: The Commanders have been blasted only twice this season — once with their backup QB playing the second half and once with their third-string rookie QB playing the majority of the game. Assuming Daniels can stay on the field for 60 minutes Sunday, I like Washington's chances to hang with a West Coast team traveling across the country to play in the early window.

By the way, the Rams' 14-point victory at Las Vegas two weeks ago? It's the only time they've won by more than four points in their last eight games outside of Los Angeles.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs describes latest abuse allegations as an 'attack,' not worried about suspension from league
articles.summary: At least three other women have accused Josh Jacobs of abuse after his arrest in May.
articles.body:
Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs addressed the new abuse allegations made against him for the first time on Wednesday afternoon.

Jacobs, who has returned to the field for the Packers in recent weeks, again denied any wrongdoing. He said the latest wave of abuse allegations, which came after his arrest earlier this year, felt like an "attack."

"It really felt like an attack on me and who I am and my character," Jacobs said, via NBC26's Kelly Hallinan. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of stuff that's being said about me that's completely false, like completely made up. People just run with it. "I can't change that … I didn't want to go to a place where I felt like I was closed off and I'm angry all the time because of what's going on in my life."

"It really felt like an attack on me and who I am and my character," Jacobs said, via NBC26's Kelly Hallinan. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of stuff that's being said about me that's completely false, like completely made up. People just run with it.

"I can't change that … I didn't want to go to a place where I felt like I was closed off and I'm angry all the time because of what's going on in my life."

New allegations made against Josh Jacobs

Jacobs was first arrested in northern Wisconsin in May and charged with multiple counts of domestic abuse. He allegedly grabbed a woman who was trying to leave his garage and threw her to the ground.

Jacobs was formally charged with battery and criminal damage to property after that incident. He pleaded no contest to both charges. Jacobs landed on the commissioner's exempt list as a result of his arrest and missed the first six games of the season.

Last week, previously unreleased files from the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department revealed that they were contacted by at least three other women accusing Jacobs of abuse.

One woman told police that Jacobs slapped her in the face and took her phone as she tried to leave his home. She said Jacobs grabbed her by the hair and throat, pinned her down on the bed and threw her onto the floor. A second woman said Jacobs grabbed her arm, pushed her up against the wall and threw items of hers outside of the home.

A third woman said Jacobs flew her to his home and later grabbed her by the head, dragged her, scratched her chest and took her phone after it fell to the floor during an altercation. The woman said she had bruising on her arm and scratches on her chest, and that she didn't report it because she feared being deported from the United States.

Jacobs has denied any wrongdoing through his attorney , and said that they have "a substantial body of tangible evidence to back up his assertions."

"Everything that my lawyer said in the statement, it's one of those things where I'm going to lean on that," Jacobs said. "It's just one of those things where it's like, anything can be said and people are just going to run with it. I can't really change how you feel. But at the end of the day, I know what I have on my part."

Jacobs returned to the field for the Packers' loss to the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25, and he had 36 yards on 11 carries in that contest. He had 29 yards on 21 carries and scored a touchdown the following week in their win against the Carolina Panthers.

The NFL is investigating the new allegations made against Jacobs, and could still hand down a suspension. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that they were letting the league process play out , but he expected that Jacobs would remain with the Packers.

Jacobs said he isn't expecting any further suspension, either.

"With all the evidence that we have and that they have, at this point it's not one of those things where I'm sitting back on my hands like, 'OK, am I going to play this week?' I kinda already know what it is," Jacobs said. "It's really just up to them to make their final decision. But I'm not worried about feeling like I'm going to miss any more time than I already have."

When Jacobs scored a touchdown against the Panthers, he celebrated in the end zone at Lambeau Field by appearing to mimic that his hands were handcuffed behind his back — something that has drawn criticism considering his recent arrest and the abuse allegations that were levied against him.

Jacobs again denied that the celebration had anything to do with his arrest, and said instead that he was referencing a gospel song.

He did, though, say he spoke with LaFleur and apologized for the extra attention that it's brought to the team.

"It wasn't my intention to make it a thing that it would be negative," Jacobs said . "The thing that I was receiving when he was walking to me was, it's not just me that has to answer for it … I told him for that, I apologize."

articles.title: Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Is On Track To Make NFL History
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is putting together a season that could place him among the most productive pass catchers in NFL history. T...
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is putting together a season that could place him among the most productive pass catchers in NFL history. The third-year standout is on pace to challenge Calvin Johnson's single-season receiving record while pursuing the league's first 2,000-yard receiving season.

The wideout continued his historic campaign Monday night, recording six receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. The performance marked his seventh game with at least 100 receiving yards through the first eight contests, placing him in rare company during the Super Bowl era.

The 24-year-old now has 985 receiving yards and nine touchdowns through eight games, putting him ahead of the rest of the NFL in receiving yardage. Smith-Njigba's current average of 123.1 yards per game projects to approximately 2,093 yards over a 17-game schedule, a total that would surpass Johnson's benchmark of 1,964 yards set with the Detroit Lions in 2012.

Johnson averaged 122.8 receiving yards per game during his record-setting season, which took place when the NFL played 16 regular-season games. At his current pace, Smith-Njigba could break that mark before the end of the 16th game, potentially making the extra game unnecessary to reach the record.

Seattle Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba On Pace To Achieve NFL History

Smith-Njigba is on track to break a record achieved by Johnson during his time in the league. This can be seen in a post made by Topps on Instagram.

The chase also puts the receiver within reach of another notable milestone. Only one player has reached 2,000 receiving yards in a season, and the Seahawks' leading pass catcher would become the first to accomplish the feat if he maintains his production. Cooper Kupp came close in 2021, finishing with 1,947 yards for the Los Angeles Rams, just 17 short of Johnson's record.

Seattle's offense has relied heavily on Smith-Njigba , whose production has continued despite opposing defenses focusing on limiting his impact. The Seahawks will need to sustain their passing-game efficiency and keep their star healthy as the schedule advances. With nine games remaining, the opportunity to rewrite the NFL record book remains within reach, although maintaining the current pace will be a significant challenge.

articles.title: Niners coach Kyle Shanahan confirms report that Vikings WR Jauan Jennings denied trade back to San Francisco
articles.summary: Shanahan said the call in which Jennings turned down the Niners actually 'went well.'
articles.body:
A trade was reportedly in place to send Minnesota Vikings receiver Jauan Jennings back to the San Francisco 49ers, his previous professional home for six seasons, until the player himself shot the deal down .

That was the story from Fox Sports' Jay Glazer on Sunday, delivering the news that Jennings made clear he did not want to return to San Francisco when asked to get on a FaceTime call with Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch:

"It was contingent upon [Jennings] hopping on a FaceTime with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch and saying, 'OK, yeah, I want to come back,' but he didn't. He said, 'Actually, no I want to stay here in Minnesota.'"

Shanahan addressed the matter Wednesday, confirming the report and telling reporters he was "not really" surprised that Jennings turned down the Niners. He did, however, emphasize the call was friendly in nature.

"The report was accurate, just not totally, exactly detailed. You can't talk to players on other teams, you're not allowed to. We love Jauan. We have such a good relationship with Jauan. I know him real well. We don't want to do it without talking to him first. We had to agree on some things to at least make it close enough to be able to talk to him. "When we got on a FaceTime with J.J., it went well. It was awesome. We talked about a lot of stuff and he ended up saying that he was happy with where he was. It wasn't just a definite no at first, but he was like, 'Kyle, I'm pretty happy here, I'm liking stuff.' When I heard the way he talked and where we're at, I agreed with him. It was a good conversation and something that was possible, but that's why it didn't go down."

Jennings played for the Niners from 2020-25, after which he signed a one-year, $8 million deal with the Vikings . His NFL career began as a seventh-round pick in the 2020 NFL Draft and he slowly saw his role expand in the Niners offense, with career years in 2024 and 2025.

That tenure wasn't without incident, as Jennings previously requested a trade following the 2024 season, which ended with a $3 million pay bump.

The Niners are looking for any receiving help they can get, as their current group of pass-catchers has been ravaged by injuries. Demarcus Robinson, De'Zhaun Stribling and Ricky Pearsall are all on injured reserve, while veterans Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. have both missed multiple games recently.

Jennings has posted only 54 receiving yards in six games for the Vikings this season, but he knows the San Francisco offense and would have been an immediately usable option. Instead, he will continue to play as the WR3 behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

articles.title: “I am lucky that whole life, I have been surrounded by people”: How one Cincinnati coach helped Jason Kelce find his NFL future with a suggestion  the Eagles legend never expected
articles.summary: Jason Kelce's NFL journey did not begin with the promise of becoming a star.
articles.body: Jason Kelce's NFL journey did not begin with the promise of becoming a star. When he joined the University of Cincinnati, he was a walk-on linebacker with no major expectations surrounding him. He had to earn his place, prove himself and find a way to keep moving forward.But one coach noticed something in him that Kelce had never considered. Strength coach Paul Longo suggested that he try playing center. It sounded like an unlikely move at the time, but it eventually changed the direction of his career. Years later, during his emotional retirement speech, Kelce made sure to remember the coach who helped him find his place in football. Paul Longo saw potential in Jason Kelce before he became a centerDuring his March 4, 2024, retirement speech at the Eagles' NovaCare Complex, Kelce looked back at his early days at Cincinnati.“From Cleveland Heights, I entered the University of Cincinnati as a walk-on. As a linebacker, I had no idea what to expect,” he recalled.He also explained how little support or recognition he had when he arrived.“I had no stars, no investment from the team or the coaches. I'd have to earn everything.”Then came a suggestion that changed his career. Kelce remembered Longo approaching him during winter workouts.“Two weeks into winter workouts, Paul whispered to me in the middle of warmups, ‘You'd make a great center,’” he said.Kelce did not immediately accept the idea. Playing on the offensive line was nowhere in his plans.“I shrugged it off. Offensive line? Never in a million years did I think I'd play that position,” he recalled.Longo, however, saw an opportunity. He moved Kelce to the offensive line that spring, giving him a chance to develop in a completely different role.Looking back, Kelce did not hide how much that decision meant to him.“Paul moved me to offensive line that spring, and it ended up being the single greatest move that ever happened to me as a football player,” he said.Longo also had a different approach to coaching. Kelce remembered his motto as, “Work smarter, not harder.” He focused on helping players become stronger, faster and more explosive instead of simply pushing them through exhausting workouts.Jason Kelce's retirement speech carried a special message for his coachThe most emotional part of Kelce's speech came when he spoke about the people who had supported him throughout his life.“I am lucky. My whole life, I have been surrounded by people that have believed in me – my father, my mother, my brother, Paul Longo, Howard Mudd,” he said.It was a meaningful mention. Longo had entered his story when Kelce was still trying to establish himself as a college football player. He saw a future in him that the young linebacker could not picture for himself.Kelce's words also showed that he had not forgotten the people who helped him along the way. His career brought him plenty of recognition, but he still made room in his final speech to acknowledge those who had backed him before the NFL spotlight arrived.The position change eventually helped him build a remarkable career. The Philadelphia Eagles selected Kelce in the sixth round of the 2011 NFL Draft. He spent 13 seasons with the franchise, earned seven Pro Bowl selections and six first-team All-Pro honours, and helped Philadelphia win Super Bowl LII.He also became one of the most respected centers of his generation.Yet, when Kelce looked back at the journey during his retirement speech, he did not only talk about the awards or the Super Bowl victory. He remembered the people who believed in him when he was still finding his way.For Longo, that quiet suggestion during a college workout became part of a much bigger story. And for Kelce, the coach who saw a center in a linebacker remained someone worth thanking years after their time together at Cincinnati.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jalen Hurts Reportedly Returns to Eagles' Facility Amid Blood Clot Recovery, Provides 'Morale Boost'
articles.summary: While Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season as he recovers from blood clots, the quarterback reportedly provided a "morale boost" for the Philadelphia Eagles on Wednesday by visiting the team facility.
articles.body:
While Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season as he recovers from blood clots, the quarterback reportedly provided a "morale boost" for the Philadelphia Eagles on Wednesday by visiting the team facility.

ESPN's Tim McManus reported Hurts returned to the facility, which was "the first time some players had seen him since he was put on injured reserve."

The quarterback didn't address the team, but McManus reported "his presence did provide a morale boost for some."

Hurts was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London ahead of Philadelphia's Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. He played in the game and flew home, although an ultrasound later discovered the blood clot moved.

The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, released a joint statement saying the official diagnosis was "deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli."

Most notably, the update said he was "clinically stable."

Its Week 8 loss to the Washington Commanders extended its losing streak to six and dropped it to 2-6 overall. At this point, it seems like the NFC East team is playing out the string on what is shaping up to be a lost season.

Still, the Eagles do have an opportunity to make up some ground on the division-leading New York Giants on Sunday.

New York is the only team above .500 in the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record.

Tanner McKee has filled in for Hurts with the starter sidelined, but McManus noted Joe Milton is expected to start against the Giants. Milton saw limited playing time as a backup for the Dallas Cowboys last season and appeared in just one game during the 2024 campaign for the New England Patriots.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts visits Eagles team facility, sits in on meetings amid recovery from blood clots
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season while dealing with multiple blood clots.
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts is not ready to make his return to the field, but he did make an appearance at the team's practice facility Wednesday.

Hurts, who has been dealing with blood clots in his lungs, sat in on the team meeting and additional smaller meetings at the team's facility Wednesday, according to ESPN's Tim McManus . Hurts did not address the team, but it marked the first time that some players had seen him since he landed on injured reserve .

"I've talked to him and am in constant communication with him and know he's resting and recovering," Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said, via ESPN. "I miss him like crazy. But nothing new on that front. I know he's resting and recovering, and we're all still praying for him and hoping for a speedy recovery."

Hurts was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and a bilateral pulmonary emboli last month, and is now expected to miss the rest of the season recovering. One blood clot is in his leg, and the other issue involves multiple blood clots in his lungs.

Hurts was placed on blood thinners and has been recovering ever since. He is expected to make a full recovery.

Hurts last played in the team's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. He was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London before that game and flew home with the team normally. After practicing with the team without restriction the following Wednesday, an ultrasound revealed that the blood clot had moved. Hurts hasn't played since.

Tanner McKee took over for Hurts in his absence, but the team has lost three straight under his watch. The Eagles announced Wednesday they will start Joe Milton at quarterback this week for Sunday's matchup with the New York Giants. It will mark the first start of Milton's NFL career.

The Eagles sit at 2-6. They've lost six in a row, dating back to before Hurts' blood clot issues.

articles.title: Justin Herbert Responds to Rams' Quentin Lake's 'Deli Meat' Comments Amid Chargers QB's Struggles
articles.summary: If Justin Herbert really is "throwing deli meat" on the field this season, the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback certainly isn't going to admit it.
articles.body:
If Justin Herbert really is "throwing deli meat" on the field this season, the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback certainly isn't going to admit it.

Herbert threw two interceptions in the team's most recent loss to the Los Angeles Rams, with one of them going to Quentin Lake. The safety turned heads during an appearance on the St. Brown Podcast when he said (h/t Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk ), "He was throwing deli meat out there. He's seeing ghosts. I don't know what's going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one."

Herbert was naturally asked about those comments, but didn't offer much of a response.

"I haven't looked into it, haven't heard anything about it, so I can't really make a comment about it," the quarterback told reporters . "We're really just focused on what's going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. And that's all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control."

Herbert wasn't the only one with the Chargers who was asked about Lake's comments.

"As far as anyone's opinion, I don't see that," Los Angeles head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters . "Everybody's entitled to their opinion, that's not what I see."

While Herbert is a two-time Pro Bowler and was considered one of the best quarterbacks in the league not long ago, it has been a season to forget to this point.

He leads the league with 10 interceptions to go with just five touchdown passes. What's more, the Chargers are an ugly 0-7 on the campaign and managed just nine points in the loss to the Rams.

It was the second straight game Los Angeles finished in single digits, as it also lost 22-6 to the Kansas City Chiefs.

There is surely no shortage of frustration for the Chargers at this point, but Herbert and Harbaugh didn't offer much of a response to the noteworthy comments from Lake.

articles.title: “Troy Aikman is not like that”: Terry Bradshaw breaks silence on Cowboys legend’s reported rift with Joe Buck over $108 million ESPN deal

articles.body: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck have spent nearly 25 years working together, but their relationship now faces questions following a reported contract dispute at ESPN. As speculation grows about a possible split, Hall of Fame quarterback Terry Bradshaw has stepped in to defend his longtime friend. He also revealed that he contacted Buck personally and does not believe money alone could explain the reported disagreement between the two broadcasters.Bradshaw's comments offer a different perspective on the controversy. While reports suggest that Buck's new $108 million contract created tension, the former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback believes Aikman is not someone who would let money damage a friendship. Terry Bradshaw stands up for Troy Aikman as Joe Buck contract dispute raises questionsBradshaw discussed the situation during an interview with FOX News host Brian Kilmeade. He revealed that he had exchanged text messages with Buck and urged him not to assume every report about the disagreement was accurate."I have talked to Buck via text and told him I don't assume everything I'm reading is correct," Bradshaw told Kilmeade.The Hall of Famer also explained why he found the reported financial disagreement difficult to believe. Both broadcasters have enjoyed successful careers, and Aikman has earned substantial money throughout his time in the NFL and broadcasting."I don't want to believe that it's the money that Buck got that's got Troy upset because Troy's making big money," Bradshaw said.He then shared what he understood about their contract negotiations. According to Bradshaw, Buck and Aikman had initially planned to approach ESPN together for new deals. However, Buck reportedly secured his extension before Aikman."I've heard that they were going to go into ESPN together and get a new deal together. Joe evidently got his before Troy. And that seems to be the rift. It's about money," he explained.Still, Bradshaw refused to believe that Aikman would allow the situation to affect their friendship."I find that hard to believe because Troy Aikman, he's not like that. And my understanding right now is things are OK," he added.However, the reported disagreement has already raised questions about what happens after the current season.Joe Buck's $108 million ESPN deal leaves Troy Aikman uncertain about his futureBuck signed a six-year extension worth $108 million with ESPN, while Aikman continues to work under the agreement he signed in 2022. Reports suggest Aikman did not know about Buck's new deal before it became public.The situation reportedly led to an argument before the October 12, 2026, Monday Night Football broadcast between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams.Buck reportedly defended himself during their disagreement, telling Aikman, "I'm not the reason you don't have a contract."Aikman later addressed his future while speaking to reporters after the controversy surfaced. He confirmed that he would complete the season before becoming a free agent."I don't know if now is the time. I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what happened. I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens," Aikman said.The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback also discussed the uncertainty during an appearance on 96.7 The Ticket Dallas."As I'm into my last year at ESPN, I'm realizing that this is something that could very well be taken away from me," Aikman said.He admitted that the situation had made him appreciate his broadcasting career even more. Aikman also expressed hope that his time in the profession was not coming to an end.The reported tension comes after the pair experienced several changes behind the scenes at ESPN. According to The Athletic, they went through five producers and directors during their first four years at the network before settling into a comfortable arrangement with Steve Ackles and Artie Kempner.For now, Buck and Aikman remain scheduled to call the 2027 Super Bowl together. articles.summary: Kelly Stafford’s complaint about the NFL schedule has drawn a sharp response from former Denver Broncos safety T.J.
articles.body: Kelly Stafford’s complaint about the NFL schedule has drawn a sharp response from former Denver Broncos safety T.J. Ward, who believes players’ wives should be more careful about what they say publicly. Ward, a Super Bowl champion, addressed Kelly’s remarks on the “Speakeasy” podcast, arguing that a player’s spouse can influence how fans and the media view him. His comments went beyond the scheduling debate, raising questions about the balance between personal expression and a football player’s public image. Kelly’s criticism came after the Los Angeles Rams received an unusual schedule around their Week 11 bye.T.J. Ward questions Kelly Stafford’s public criticismKelly Stafford had raised concerns about the Rams’ schedule, saying her husband Matthew Stafford’s team would not receive a “true bye week.” The Rams play on November 15, take their bye on November 22, and then return for a game on November 25.That leaves the team with only 10 days between games, rather than the usual 14-day gap teams get when they play on Sundays before and after a bye. Kelly, who has spent 18 years around the NFL, also highlighted the toll the schedule takes on those watching from the sidelines.“After 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap,” she wrote. She added, “I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel.”Ward, who won a Super Bowl with Denver, took issue with her decision to share those thoughts publicly. He said, “Outside of family members, your wife is the biggest extension of you.”He then made his stance clear: “At some point, we have to tell the wives to get off Twitter. Get off. We understand your feelings; whether right or wrong, you reflect me in the biggest and most important ways. Whatever you say might as well come out of my mouth and be on my Twitter. Get the wives off of Twitter; it’s damaging.”Ward says players’ wives reflect their husbandsWard’s argument centered on how a spouse’s comments can affect a player’s reputation. He believes that when an NFL wife criticizes a team or the league, people may assume her husband shares the same view, even if he has said nothing publicly.He expanded on that point with a remark that could draw further attention: “It’s like you have no control at home,” Ward added. “She says whatever she wants; she does whatever she wants. I know that sounds crazy because, as individuals, you have that right. But if I have to watch what I say on Twitter and within the organization, then you, you watch what you say because you are a reflection of me.”The comments shift the focus from the Rams’ schedule to the expectations placed on players’ families. Ward’s view is that a public statement from a spouse can carry consequences inside the league, where players are expected to manage their own words carefully.Kelly’s complaint, however, was about the demands of the schedule and the limited recovery time it creates. The disagreement highlights a tension between an NFL player’s public image and a spouse’s right to speak openly about the league.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘You can’t win a Super Bowl…’: Calvin Johnson revisits Lions’ biggest mistake
articles.summary: Calvin Johnson believes the Detroit Lions have had the talent to win a Super Bowl but insists they cannot reach the NFL’s biggest prize without being willing...
articles.body:
Calvin Johnson believes the Detroit Lions have had the talent to win a Super Bowl but insists they cannot reach the NFL's biggest prize without being willing to spend big.

The former wide receiver pointed to Matthew Stafford's departure as an example of why Detroit needed to be more aggressive in building a championship-winning roster.

Johnson spent his entire NFL career with the Lions before retiring at just 30 years old, but his relationship with the organisation has improved considerably in recent years.

Calvin Johnson says Detroit Lions cannot win Super Bowl on a budget

Speaking on the Chasing No. 1 podcast, Johnson explained why he believed Detroit had the necessary pieces during his time with the franchise.

"The biggest thing for me is that, I used to always say, we tell everybody we got the team here in Detroit. We had the dudes, but you can't win a Super Bowl on a budget, man. You got to go all in."

Johnson also pointed to teams making significant moves to add the final pieces needed to compete for a championship.

He then brought up Stafford, who won the Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams in his first season after leaving Detroit.

"We had most of the pieces there in Detroit. And so for me, when he won Super Bowl, literally the first year after he left Detroit, I'm out there like, 'I mean, I told y'all what we had.'"

Stafford's success with the Rams reinforced Johnson's belief that the Lions had been closer to competing for a title than their lack of championship success suggested.

With the NFL trade deadline approaching, Detroit fans are hoping general manager Brad Holmes can strengthen the roster as the team looks to maintain its position in the NFC North.

Johnson's comments also come after years of tension between him and the Lions following his retirement.

The organisation once sought $1.6 million back from his signing bonus after he walked away before completing his contract. However, those differences have since faded.

Johnson has returned to Ford Field to support the team and has earned places on the Lions' All-Time Team and Ring of Honor.

Now, with Detroit still chasing its first Super Bowl title, his message remains clear: having the talent is not enough if the organisation is unwilling to make the moves needed to finish the job.

articles.title: Packers’ dreadful running game will finally come back to bite them vs. red-hot Drake Maye, Patriots
articles.summary: Week 9 in the NFL is a bit of a sleepy slate, but the afternoon window on Sunday presents one titanic battle between two playoff contenders. Two of the most...
articles.body:
Week 9 in the NFL is a bit of a sleepy slate, but the afternoon window on Sunday presents one titanic battle between two playoff contenders. Two of the most storied franchises in the NFL will do battle when the Green Bay Packers travel to Foxborough to take on the New England Patriots .

Both teams come into this game at 5-3 , but both are behind in their respective division races. That makes this game crucial both for wild card positioning as well as the races in the NFC North and AFC East.

Interestingly, both the Packers and the Patriots have had similar arcs so far this season. Both teams looked down and out after starting 1-2, and both had massive issues on the offensive side of the ball they had to fix. Drake Maye was turning the ball over at will for the Pats, and the Packers had massive offensive line woes to fix.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Since then, both teams are 4-1 and are starting to look more and more like the squads that many pegged as playoff teams before the season. Both still have some flaws, but the explosiveness of both teams should make this an entertaining, back-and-forth contest on Sunday.

Most things with the Packers start with their lack of a running game, and this game should be no different. How else can Green Bay attack, and what is it up against on the other side?

Don't expect the Packers' run game to be revived this week

Not only do the Packers have the worst running game in the NFL, but they have one of the worst running games in the league in recent memory. The numbers almost seem fake: last in yards per rush (2.9), last in EPA per rush (-0.26), last in success rate (30.6%), and 30th in stuff rate (20.6%) per Next Gen Stats. They also rank 30th in both yards before and after contact, so everyone shares the blame for the issues on the ground.

The Green Bay offensive line, which has weathered a number of injuries and gotten back to at least a competent level in the passing game, has remained a dismal mess on the ground. They don't get push off the ball and don't climb to the second level effectively, allowing second- and third-level defenders to come unscathed and make plays near the line of scrimmage.

The backs haven't helped matters, though getting Josh Jacobs back should help in that department. MarShawn Lloyd, who was getting a lot of the work for the Packers before Jacobs returned from the Commissioner's Exempt List, has forced just 11 missed tackles on 57 attempts according to PFF, which just isn't going to cut it (Jahmyr Gibbs leads the league with 51).

Jacobs being back will make things a little bit better. He is a more physical runner and a better receiver than Lloyd or Pierre Strong Jr., but he still has only forced two missed tackles on 32 attempts in his first two games. While he may not give Green Bay more explosiveness than it already had, the Packers posted their two lowest stuff rates of the season in the two games that he played. That isn't a coincidence.

Things are unlikely to get any better on Sunday against a Patriots defense that ranks in the top 10 in both EPA per rush allowed and yards per rush allowed, per Next Gen Stats. Mike Vrabel and company boast one of the best interior duos in football in Christian Barmore and Milton Williams, and the numbers bear that out. The Pats allow the second fewest yards before contact (0.57) in the NFL, as they dominate the line of scrimmage with those two guys and get ballcarriers on the ground quickly.

Can Jordan Love play Houdini on obvious passing downs again?

If the Packers are once again unable to run the ball in this game, that puts Jordan Love in a position where he is going to have to play Superman for this Packers offense once again. Considering the situation around him, Love is quietly having one of the best seasons of any quarterback in the NFL. He leads the league in passing yards with 2,246 and is fourth in passing touchdowns with 16.

As he usually does, Love is chucking the ball all over the yard and hunting explosive plays for this Green Bay offense. His 9.5 air yards per attempt is the third-highest in the NFL per Next Gen Stats, trailing only C.J. Stroud and Malik Willis.

But in this game, Love is going to have to find some answers against a talented Patriots secondary that will make it very hard on them, especially on the outside. That will only get more difficult in the obvious passing situations that will be created by the lack of a running game on early downs. However, on second- and third-and-long, Love ranks in the top 10 in EPA per dropback.

Second-and-long is going to be a key down in this game on this side of the ball. Green Bay has run the most plays on second-and-long in the NFL this season, in large part due to the aforementioned issues on the ground. The Packers have the fourth-highest pass rate on those plays, and the Patriots have been a bit vulnerable on those snaps this season. New England is allowing 7.2 yards per play on second-and-long passing plays, the seventh-highest number in football per Next Gen Stats.

On second-and-long, defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr loves to dial up the blitz. The Patriots' 42.9% blitz rate on those downs is the second-highest rate in the league, trailing only Brian Flores and the Minnesota Vikings (who else?). But Love has more attempts and yards against the blitz than any other quarterback this season, so he will be ready for it.

The last thing that is key in every Packers game is slowing down Green Bay's deep passing game. Love throws the ball 20 or more yards down the field on 14.7% of his throws, the second-highest number in football. While it hasn't been all that fruitful so far in 2026, in part due to some drops, Love has two emerging stars in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to target on those throws.

The Patriots rank in the middle of the pack against deep passes, both in terms of counting stats and efficiency numbers. That could be an area that the Packers look to exploit on Sunday.

On the other side of the ball, Drake Maye is looking like the guy who nearly won the MVP in his second season in the NFL. After a slow start to the season, Maye is now playing his best football and is leading one of the best passing games in the NFL despite a plethora of injuries to his wide receivers .

Even when you factor in Maye's early-season struggles, where he had one touchdown and six interceptions in his first three games, he still ranks in the top 10 in the NFL in EPA per dropback, passing touchdowns and yards per attempt.

On the other side, Jonathan Gannon has quietly turned this Packers group into a very good pass defense. Green Bay ranks third in the NFL in yards per pass allowed, seventh in EPA per pass allowed, and fifth in pressure rate according to Next Gen Stats. Gannon has started to get a very good feel for his personnel in Green Bay, knowing when to heat opposing quarterbacks up and when to lay back and play coverage. Sending pressure packages worked in games like a win over the Cowboys, when Dak Prescott and the Dallas offense were completely flummoxed all game long in Week 6.

When Green Bay does get pressure on Maye on Sunday, and it very likely will plenty of times against a Patriots offensive line that has been leaky so far this season, it will be interesting to see how effective they can be at slowing him down.

Maye has been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL when pressured so far this season. His EPA per dropback on those snaps is the second-best mark in the NFL, trailing only Patrick Mahomes. He is second in the NFL in yards this season when under pressure as well, so he is no stranger to working with defenders around him in the backfield. Look for Maye to come up big in the face of pressure when the Patriots really need a big play on Sunday.
