articles.title: “We put him through as much stress as we can": Raiders’ Klint Kubiak reveals what Fernando Mendoza must prove before taking over from Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have found an unexpected advantage in Kirk Cousins, whose strong start to the 2026 season has given the team stability at
articles.body: The Las Vegas Raiders have found an unexpected advantage in Kirk Cousins, whose strong start to the 2026 season has given the team stability at quarterback. His performances have also allowed rookie Fernando Mendoza to develop without being rushed into the starting role. However, head coach Klint Kubiak wants the No. 1 overall pick to be ready whenever his opportunity arrives. Kubiak recently offered an insight into how the coaching staff is preparing Mendoza, making it clear that limited playing time will not lower expectations for the young quarterback.Klint Kubiak puts Fernando Mendoza under pressure during Raiders practicesMendoza entered the NFL with considerable expectations after the Raiders selected him with the first overall pick. The team wanted a young quarterback who could become its long-term leader, but it also understood the value of bringing in an experienced player to guide him through his first professional season.Cousins has turned out to be an excellent option. Despite questions about his future following an underwhelming spell with the Atlanta Falcons, the veteran has delivered impressive numbers in Las Vegas. Through his first eight games with the Raiders, he ranks second in the NFL with 19 passing touchdowns and third with 2,124 passing yards. The team is also holding a 4-4 record heading into Week 9.That production has made it difficult for the coaching staff to consider a change at quarterback. Cousins understands Kubiak's system and has given the Raiders a reliable option while Mendoza continues learning from the sidelines.Kubiak, however, does not want the rookie to mistake his backup role for a reduced level of responsibility. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, the Raiders head coach explained how the staff is testing Mendoza's readiness despite his limited opportunities to work with the first team.“I think when you are the backup quarterback and you don’t get a ton of reps, I think we all find out together on Sunday how ready he is,” Kubiak said of Mendoza. “We put him through as much stress as we can. Coach [Mike] Sullivan does a phenomenal job, coach Andrew [Janocko], and when his time is called, whether he gets three more years of reps or he gets one more day of reps, he has to be ready.”The message is straightforward. Mendoza may not receive the same number of practice opportunities as Cousins, but the coaching staff expects him to handle the pressure when called upon. An injury, a sudden change in form or an unexpected game situation could put the rookie in charge without much warning.Kubiak has repeatedly backed Cousins as the starter, leaving little doubt about the current quarterback hierarchy. Mendoza has already received some playing time this season, giving the Raiders an early look at his potential. Still, his biggest test will come when he has to manage an entire game.Kirk Cousins explains his approach to handling pressureCousins has offered more than just production during his first season in Las Vegas. His experience has also helped the Raiders navigate difficult situations, including their comeback victory over the New York Jets.The veteran threw three touchdown passes and added a rushing score as Las Vegas recovered from a nine-point deficit to win 38-31. His ability to remain composed played a major role in the result.Cousins recently explained how he approaches those moments.“I’ve always tried not to ride the roller coaster,” Cousins said. “But for the most part, I just try to be steady because I know in this league there are going to be ups and downs. Just stay the course and keep playing. … You’ve just got to believe that if you keep playing, there’s a good chance you’ll be right there in the fourth quarter.”That mindset is one of the qualities Mendoza can observe while learning behind him. Cousins will now face another challenge against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 9, with the Raiders looking to improve to 5-4.For Mendoza, the immediate task remains preparation rather than waiting for a starting opportunity. Cousins is giving Las Vegas results, but Kubiak's message suggests the rookie will be judged on how well he responds when the team needs him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: The Green Bay Packers were 4-2 and the Detroit Lions 3-2 before their Week 7 matchup in the 2026 NFL season. A win would have made the Packers 5-2, a loss 4-3.For the Lions, a win would have made them 4-2, a loss 3-3. Somehow, the NFL referees reportedly influenced the game, and Detroit beat Green Bay.Otherwise, why would Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson report on X that the officiating crew responsible for several bad calls in the Packers vs. Lions game was moved from NBC’s Sunday primetime game [Eagles vs. Commanders] to the Dolphins vs. Patriots game [regional broadcast] for “optic reasons”- this is like saying, we’re sorry for your loss, but we’ve fixed what caused it so other teams don’t suffer the same fate.This clearly didn’t sit well with Packers quarterback Jordan Love. The wrongly called game took place on October 25, and Love and his wife, Ronika Stone, reportedly made full use of it for Halloween 2026 by dressing up as blind referees!Jordan Love wants to win more than achieve career goalsGreen Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love leads the league in passing yards - 2246 - but this is not what he cares about. “It’s a cool stat, but no, I think my job is to go out there and be the best player, throw for a lot of yards; the main goal is to win the game.However you get that done, you get that done,”he said after Nov. 4 practice.It’s not about the stats he accumulates; it’s always about winning every week of the NFL season. That didn’t happen in Green Bay’s controversial Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions.So he turned their Halloween 2026 celebrations into a befitting criticism of NFL officiating.The NFL power couple dressed as visually impaired referees, expressing their frustration over questionable decisions in the Week 7 defeat.Some fans loved how quickly he channeled his creativity for Halloween, while others feared he might face disciplinary action for mocking NFL officials.Jordan Love and Ronika Stone’s Halloween referee costumesNFL quarterback Jordan Love and former professional volleyball player Ronika Stone wore traditional black-and-white striped referee uniforms. They accessorized with dark sunglasses and carried white mobility canes.Ronika Stone Love shared a TikTok video showing both of them walking around. At one point, they collided and fell to the ground. They even threw yellow penalty flags.The NFL WAG captioned the post, “I’m jokin, immmmmm jokin.” When their costumes sparked discussions about their intentions, Stone clarified in the comments, saying, “We’re Footlocker employees.”The video highlighted the couple’s dissatisfaction with the decisions that led NFL officiating to declare Week 7 a defeat. They also made sure not to accuse any particular referee of wrongdoing. But what were the “bad” calls?Lions vs Packers officiating controversy explainedThe Green Bay Packers lost to the Detroit Lions 20-17 on October 25. The Packers had 8 penalties for 81 yards during the Sunday matchup.Packers defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt suggested NFL officials favored Detroit. Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged several difficult calls.Packers safety Xavier McKinney questioned why Detroit’s defenders received different treatment when they hit his QB Jordan Love. The league fined him $25,000 for his stern criticism.Later, Green Bay admitted missed scoring opportunities caused the Week 7 defeat. They managed just 7 points on 4 red-zone possessions.Jordan Love’s NFL penalty frustrationsThrough the first eight weeks of the 2026 NFL season, Jordan Love has faced an uphill battle. As Barstool Sports recently highlighted, the Packers’ struggling offensive line and inconsistent rushing attack have forced Love to carry the offense under immense duress.According to PackersNews, he has already absorbed 46 hits and 14 sacks, making him one of the most battered quarterbacks in the league - a physical toll that ultimately resulted in a back injury during Week 6 against Dallas.Making matters worse, Jordan Love has endured this punishment without a single roughing-the-passer penalty called in his favor, a frustrating reality for a discipline-heavy Green Bay team that already leads the NFL with 591 penalty yards.Yet, despite these brutal hurdles, Love has been spectacular, leading the league with 2,246 passing yards and 16 touchdowns.With the viral drama of his ‘blind referee’Halloween costume behind him - and hopefully no league fines incoming - all eyes now turn to how he navigates these challenges in a crucial Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce exposes Kylie Kelce's no-filter side with a candid admission about their Chiefs-Eagles rivalry
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has learned that family ties do not always translate into football support.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has learned that family ties do not always translate into football support. His sister-in-law, Kylie Kelce, remains firmly committed to the Philadelphia Eagles, even when her brother-in-law is on the opposite side. During a recent episode of New Heights, Travis recalled how openly Kylie expresses that loyalty, including a blunt message she would deliver directly to him. The conversation began with a debate about another NFL team's loyalties, but it soon offered a fresh glimpse into the Kelce family's approach to football rivalries.Travis Kelce appreciates Kylie's blunt Eagles loyaltyThe exchange came as Jason Kelce questioned podcast staffer Jake Chatzky, popularly known as Jets Jake, about his loyalties ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs' upcoming matchup against the New York Jets. Chatzky grew up supporting New York, but working on a podcast hosted by Travis put him in an awkward position.When Jason asked which team he would support, Chatzky tried to avoid upsetting either side. “Don't make me do this, Jason,” he said before adding, “I'm absolutely rooting for Travis, for sure, I am 100% rooting for Travis.”Travis was not convinced. He called the staffer a “phony” and challenged his attempt to support both sides. “You hear that, Jets fans?” he said. “He's a f*cking phony. He's a phony.”When Chatzky suggested that backing Travis did not necessarily mean rooting against the Jets, Travis pushed back again. “Don't f*cking lie to my face,” he said.That was when Kylie became his example of someone who never hides her football allegiance. “At least my sister-in-law will tell me to my face, ‘F*ck you, I hope the Birds win,’” Travis said.The remark drew laughter from Jason and the podcast crew. It also showed that Travis has little problem with Kylie's refusal to put family ahead of her support for Philadelphia. He seems to value that honesty more than a polite show of support.Kylie's Eagles support has never depended on TravisKylie's loyalty was also evident at Super Bowl LVIII in February 2024, when the Chiefs faced the San Francisco 49ers. She attended the game to support Travis but refused to wear Kansas City merchandise. Instead, she chose a red University of Cincinnati shirt, a nod to the college attended by both Kelce brothers. She also wore an “Alright Nah” shirt underneath, referencing Travis.Jason had previously explained that even having family on the field could not persuade Kylie to wear Chiefs gear. “I have tried [saying], ‘Kylie, we have family in the game, it's okay to cheer on that team. They're not playing the Eagles. You realize this isn't against the Eagles, right?’ She just refuses,” Jason said on New Heights.Travis, however, took no offence. “I respect it, Ky,” he said. “I appreciate you even wearing red. You could have worn something neutral and just showed your support. You showing up was enough for me, so I appreciate it.”That response says as much about their relationship as Kylie's language does. She can support Travis as family without pretending to support his team. For the Chiefs tight end, her presence matters, even if her cheers belong elsewhere.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Next week": Dianna Russini may be ready to reclaim her NFL career as Mike Florio reveals what could happen next
articles.summary: Dianna Russini is planning a return to work next week, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio reports.
articles.body: Dianna Russini is planning a return to work next week, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio reports. It would come almost seven months after she left The Athletic over her undisclosed relationship with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. A source says she has started telling people around the league. No employer has been named. Page Six adds that she will host her own show on a digital platform, with a focus on interviews rather than breaking news. Her comeback also arrives with a review of her work, released in September, still fresh.Dianna Russini plans to return to work next weekFlorio broke down the news on Pro Football Talk. “Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she’ll be returning to work ‘next week,’” he wrote.He could not say who she will work for or what the role looks like.Page Six supplied part of the answer on Wednesday. Its report says Russini will front her own show on a digital platform that has not been identified. She “plans to interview players and coaches on her new show.” That suggests a quieter format than the one that built her name. For years she was known for scoops. Sit-down interviews are a different craft, and a safer one while questions about her past still follow her around. Interviews also keep the focus on her guests, which may be the point.Florio sees one clear hurdle. “If she’ll be reporting again, she’ll need to restore her own credibility,” he wrote. An interview show could let her rebuild that at her own pace. Whether audiences allow it is another question.How Dianna Russini's exit from The Athletic unfoldedRussini had been one of the more recognizable NFL insiders in the business. She resigned on April 14, one week after Page Six published photographs of her with Vrabel at an Arizona resort. An internal investigation followed. Her resignation letter included the line “I stand behind every story I have ever published,” and she rejected any suggestion of wrongdoing.The Athletic released its findings in September. The outlet said the undisclosed relationship broke its standards, whether or not it was romantic. It also took issue with how she handled the first questions about the photos.The review then went through her body of work: 903 written stories, 204 podcast episodes, 77 videos and other appearances. It found no clear evidence that she used her platform to promote Vrabel or his teams. Editor’s notes were added to four pieces, one story and three videos. The vast majority of her output raised no concerns.That gives her a real talking point with any new employer. The conduct drew criticism. The journalism mostly held up. What she says about all of it once the microphone is on may decide how far this comeback goes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 6 NFL Teams That Should Be the Biggest Buyers at the 2026 Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Every year, before the NFL trade deadline, playoff-contending teams make moves to shore up roster weaknesses or keep pace in division races. While some clubs will stand pat, expect some activity in the coming days, with notable names in the rumor mill.
articles.body:
Every year, before the NFL trade deadline, playoff-contending teams make moves to shore up roster weaknesses or keep pace in division races. While some clubs will stand pat, expect some activity in the coming days, with notable names in the rumor mill.

The Seattle Seahawks acquired three-time first-team All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. Days later, the Chicago Bears traded two first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for 2025 All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. These teams may have set the tone for a busy trade deadline.

So, let's look at six teams that should be the biggest buyers in the days leading up to November 10, and whom they could target to improve their playoff chances.

The Cincinnati Bengals field the league's second-ranked scoring offense with the No. 1 passing attack in total yards, but they need balance on that side of the ball.

Cincinnati is averaging the third-fewest rushing yards per game while logging 3.7 yards per carry, which ranks 28th in the league.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Bengals are one of several teams aggressively pursuing three-time Pro Bowler and 2021 rushing champion Jonathan Taylor.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler spoke to executives who think Taylor is worth a second-rounder and additional picks, but he believes the Indianapolis Colts could demand the "equivalent of a first-round pick."

If the Bengals aren't willing to meet the Colts' asking price for Taylor, ESPN's Adam Schefter suggested they could shift their attention to New York Jets running back Breece Hall.

Hall signed a three-year, $43.5 million extension this past offseason, but general manager Darren Mougey traded two-time All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner almost four months after signing him to a new deal. If Cincinnati proposes a deal he can't refuse, Hall could be a trade option.

The Bengals should also pursue a cornerback who can join Dax Hill and DJ Turner II in shoring up their 26th-ranked pass defense.

Potential trade targets: RB Jonathan Taylor, RB Breece Hall, CB Donte Jackson

The Detroit Lions could soon have their All-Pro/Pro Bowl safety duo back together. In Week 7, Brian Branch returned to action from a torn Achilles. Kerby Joseph hasn't played a snap since October of last year because of a knee injury, but he's back at practice.

Still, the Lions need to strengthen their perimeter pass coverage with an experienced veteran who can play opposite D.J. Reed.

In his age-30 season, Rock Ya-Sin is a rotational cornerback. Third-year pro Ennis Rakestraw Jr. has only played 157 defensive snaps in 13 career games (two starts). Roger McCreary has taken most of his snaps in the slot, and he's allowed three touchdowns and a 104.3 passer rating in coverage.

Furthermore, Detroit lost Jack Campbell to a neck injury that hospitalized him last week. Fortunately, head coach Dan Campbell received positive news about the All-Pro linebacker's condition.

The Lions won't rush Campbell back. So, depending on how the linebacker corps performs against the Miami Dolphins in Week 9, they could be in the market for help at that position.

The Lions have a balanced offense, with passing and rushing attacks that rank in the top seven in total yards, but they need to bolster their defense.

Potential trade targets: CB Riq Woolen, CB Kristian Fulton, LB Cedric Gray

For the past few years, the Kansas City Chiefs have needed a reliable pass-catcher to spark their passing game, and that hasn't changed this season.

Rashee Rice has missed 24 games since the 2024 campaign. Xavier Worthy, a 2024 first-rounder, hasn't taken a third-year leap to become a well-rounded receiver. The speedy wideout is averaging a career-low 8.5 yards per catch.

Tight end Travis Kelce leads the Chiefs in multiple receiving categories with 29 receptions for 410 yards and two touchdowns, but relying heavily on a 37-year-old in his 14th season is risky.

In Week 4, deep-threat wide receiver Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle and tore ligaments. Without his big-play ability, Kansas City's aerial attack will lack explosive plays.

Rice is on an expiring contract, so the Chiefs should pursue a young wideout who can take on a big role as one of Patrick Mahomes' primary targets. General manager Brett Veach should have Brian Thomas Jr. and Josh Downs at the top of his trade-acquisition list. Rashod Bateman and Jerry Jeudy are alternative options still in their prime.

Potential trade targets: WR Brian Thomas Jr., WR Josh Downs, WR Jerry Jeudy

Minnesota Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz may start on Monday against the Buffalo Bills.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , "it is trending towards" Wentz starting over Kyler Murray, who's dealing with a hamstring injury.

The Vikings will host the Bills in a battle between two one-loss teams, a good spot for Wentz to show he's a better option than Murray to lead the Vikings' offense. The 33-year-old journeyman led Minnesota in a comeback win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, throwing three touchdown passes.

In six games, Murray has thrown for 1,022 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions. Excluding the season opener, when he exited with a concussion, the eight-year pro has completed less than 59 percent of his passes in three of his five starts.

The Athletic's Ted Nguyen pointed out that Murray is "constantly late" on his reads, which has hurt his accuracy. The Vikings could bench him in favor of Wentz going forward and pursue a younger veteran signal-caller, like San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Mac Jones.

If the Vikings move forward with Murray or Wentz, they should upgrade their 17th-ranked rushing attack to ease pressure on the quarterback. Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason are serviceable, but the former turns 32 in December, and the latter currently averages 3.9 yards per carry.

Like several other teams, the Vikings should look at available top-tier running backs, though it also makes sense to add veteran quarterback insurance, since Murray is inefficient when healthy and is now nursing an injury.

Potential trade targets: RB Jonathan Taylor, RB Breece Hall, QB Mac Jones

Head coach John Harbaugh is leading an immediate turnaround in his first year with the New York Giants, though Big Blue shouldn't be complacent. The Giants have a plus-two point differential, showing the need to improve across the roster as they find consistency.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, Harbaugh reached out directly to Tennessee Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about trading for Jeffery Simmons.

"Multiple sources tell The Athletic the Giants' head coach called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk directly in an attempt to trade for the All-Pro defensive tackle, breaking with traditional NFL trade-talk norms," Jones wrote.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler still believes the Giants will bolster their defensive front and have two-time Pro Bowler Vita Vea in mind. This past offseason, the Buccaneers signed Vea to a one-year, $30 million extension, so it may take an aggressive offer to pry him away, though the Giants clearly want defensive help.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz also mentioned Big Blue among teams showing strong interest in Jonathan Taylor, which makes sense given Cam Skattebo's ball-security issues this season and Tyrone Tracy Jr.'s stint on short-term injured reserve.

Potential trade targets: RB Jonathan Taylor, RB Tony Pollard, NT Vita Vea

The Pittsburgh Steelers have strung together four consecutive wins, but their offense is mediocre, ranking 18th in scoring, 19th in total yards and tied for 19th in yards per play.

As in recent years, the Steelers are stout defensively, but they need an offensive spark. Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle have become an effective running back duo over the previous few weeks. The tandem racked up 199 rushing yards against the Cleveland Browns in Pittsburgh's last outing.

However, the Steelers won't be able to sustain offensive momentum without better balance and more help alongside lead receiver DK Metcalf. He's been inconsistent, with a career-low 51.6 percent catch rate and four drops.

Meanwhile, wideouts Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are on short-term injured reserve. Rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard has shown promising flashes, catching 32 passes for 284 yards and a touchdown, but he racked up just 57 receiving yards over Pittsburgh's last two outings.

Looking ahead to potential playoff matchups, the Steelers need another healthy wide receiver who can threaten opposing defenses to compete against the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars, who field top-five scoring offenses.

Pittsburgh should make calls on several wide receivers up until Tuesday's deadline. Keep in mind that Aaron Rodgers said this will be his last season . The Steelers should go for all the glory with a big trade that gives them a chance to make a deep run before they have to address quarterback uncertainty.

Potential trade targets: WR Brian Thomas Jr., WR Josh Downs, WR Quentin Johnston

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 9 Tips, Trade Value Rankings for Top 50 Players
articles.summary: It's time for the weekly fantasy football trade value chart, as trade deadlines across fantasy football grow closer.
articles.body:
It's time for the weekly fantasy football trade value chart, as trade deadlines across fantasy football grow closer.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a descending trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

If you have Ashton Jeanty on your roster right now, you are panicking, and that is understandable. But is it possible his fantasy value won't completely crater for you going forward? Or should you be trying to move on, even if it means selling low?

There are mixed opinions and thoughts on Sunday's demotion, though it's not looking great.

There are a few reasons why you should probably lean toward holding onto Jeanty rather than selling low.

The first one is evident enough—you'll be selling at the absolute basement of his value. Unless one of your league mates doesn't pay attention to NFL news, you're not getting back great offers.

There's also the fact that Jeanty has maintained value in a pass-catching role in PPR formats. Even if Sunday's troubling splits continue, Jeanty is probably flex-worthy off his receiving impact alone.

And it's very possible that some of Sunday's platoon splits are about Jeanty not being completely healthy. It's also a positive sign for those rooting for Jeanty to eventually regain his feature-back role that Mike Washington Jr. only rushed for 83 yards despite getting 25 carries. As Bill Barnwell of ESPN noted, Washington "managed zero rush yards over expectation, per NFL Next Gen Stats, suggesting that he got roughly what was blocked without much more."

Not exactly the sort of performance that screams "This is my job now and you aren't getting it back."

But there is a format where you might want to consider cutting ties with Jeanty at this point, even if it means selling low, and that's in dynasty. Consider this from Barnwell: "Jeanty ranks last in EPA per carry and second-to-last in success rate on the ground since entering the league."

Jeanty's done enough in the short term as a pass-catcher this season to avoid selling low in redraft formats if you can come to terms with him potentially having his upside capped at being a flex consideration. In dynasty formats, however, it's possible in the future that his value will crater even further if he can't prove to be a more reliable runner.

The counter-argument to that, of course, is that the Raiders haven't exactly had an elite offensive line in his two seasons and more patience is warranted. That's a fair take, though it presumes the Raiders will successfully draft or sign upgrades to the offensive line in free agency.

But it's evident now, more than ever, that Jeanty has become a long-term gamble in fantasy. His future may be in a platoon, and that isn't what you signed up for when you drafted him. At the moment, however, you probably don't have a great exit strategy.

articles.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Cheat Sheet for Best Values and Top Sleepers
articles.summary: Week 9 will begin with a Thursday matchup that looked better a few weeks ago than it does now. The Jacksonville Jaguars will visit the Baltimore Ravens, who won't have starting quarterback Lamar Jackson or backup Tyler Huntley because of injuries.
articles.body:
Week 9 will begin with a Thursday matchup that looked better a few weeks ago than it does now. The Jacksonville Jaguars will visit the Baltimore Ravens, who won't have starting quarterback Lamar Jackson or backup Tyler Huntley because of injuries.

The Ravens are hoping that they get enough out of rookie Joe Fagnano to keep pace with the Jags. Likewise, many fantasy managers are hoping that they can navigate Week 9 with a roster full of sleepers and waiver-wire pickups.

Injuries continue to be a scourge on the fantasy football landscape. The Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans are also on bye this week.

Here, you'll find updated point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for Week 9, a cheat sheet for value plays, and a look at some top sleeper options who may still be available on the wire.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

Waiver Target: J.J. McCarthy, QB, New York Giants

Considering how inconsistently he played with the Minnesota Vikings, J.J. McCarthy has been a very pleasant surprise for the New York Giants. In his first start with New York, the Michigan product helped deliver an overtime victory over the Houston Texans.

Of course, McCarthy didn't do much for fantasy managers in Week 7, finishing with just 10.2 fantasy points.

However, McCarthy has a very good chance to rebound this week against the rival Philadelphia Eagles. The Giants are coming off their bye and have had extra time to prepare for Vic Fangio's defense. That defense, meanwhile, has largely underwhelmed.

The Eagles have surrendered the 10th-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season. McCarthy is rostered in only 14 percent of leagues.

Teams That Should Buy at Trade Deadline 🤝

Waiver Target: Caleb Douglas, WR, Miami Dolphins

Miami Dolphins receiver Caleb Douglas isn't a weekly must-start just yet. However, the rookie has largely served as Malik Willis' go-to perimeter target when healthy and has flashed a ton of upside.

Douglas logged 14.4 fantasy points in Week 1 and recorded 21 points in Week 7. While he's coming off a modest 8.3-point outing, he should be viewed as a strong streamer moving forward.

This week, Douglas will have a must-start-caliber matchup. The Dolphins are set to host the Detroit Lions, who have surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season. Given Detroit's ability to put points on the board while defending the run well, Douglas should see a high volume of targets.

Douglas is rostered in only 25 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: B/R's Initial 2027 NHL Mock Draft Top 10
articles.summary: Happy first 2027 NHL Mock Draft! In the grand tradition of getting to the party early, we're not tackling the entire round just yet—we're looking at a potential top-10.
articles.body:
Happy first 2027 NHL Mock Draft! In the grand tradition of getting to the party early, we're not tackling the entire round just yet—we're looking at a potential top-10.

We want to focus on those early underperforming teams and give their fans a glimpse of what might be ahead if things don't improve.

(We're rooting for you to get wins instead of high picks, we promise.)

Some meaningless stats for you before we dive in: half the players in this mock Top 10 are centers. We weren't joking when we said it's a center-heavy top pool this year. There are also two players named Brock. Yes, both of them come from the WHL.

Other than the center situation, there's a pretty healthy mix all around this season, at least here at the beginning—a nice scramble of different leagues, good balance of guys playing in North America and playing overseas. Nothing feels like it's leaning too heavily in one direction right now. Obviously, we've got an entire season ahead of us, so stay tuned.

No prizes for guessing who the first overall pick is—it's a gimme—but stick around beyond that. The rest of these guys are twisted up like an unsolved Rubik's Cube.

1. Vancouver Canucks: Landon DuPont, D, Michigan (NCAA)

We're kicking things off from a very familiar place. Difficult though it may be for Vancouver Canucks fans to believe that they'll win the draft lottery, our mocks—especially this early—go by standings, so right now, you're up.

Good news for you, though, Canucks fans: Landon DuPont is the real deal. And that's a relief for a team still keenly feeling the loss of the kind of talent Quinn Hughes brought to the ice each night. While this draft year is another that is largely potential-based, rather than having a gaggle of true game-changers, DuPont is the standout who could make an impact sooner rather than later. He would be an excellent acquisition.

It's not even close—right now—in terms of the gap between pick one and pick two. DuPont took the CHL-to-NCAA path we're going to see more and more, and from the moment he stepped onto the ice for the Wolverines, he's made it clear that he is the guy to beat this year. He's eating heavy minutes, running the top power-play, and currently scoring at a point-per-game pace. Not sure he could've chosen a better development environment in which to prove he's ready to go first overall.

2. Chicago Blackhawks: Nazar Privalov, LW, CSKA Moscow (KHL)

We know the Chicago Blackhawks don't shy away from drafting Russian players, and with multiple potential high picks out of the KHL this season, CSKA Moscow forward Nazar Privalov feels like a tailor-made fit.

He's a tank of a player—6'4" and 227 pounds—and, in a trend that is becoming all the more common, he pairs that size with highly effective offensive skill.

Privalov brings a powerful attacking style that the Blackhawks will both value and need moving forward. He's more direct than deceptive when it comes to creating offense, but don't mistake that for a lack of playmaking ability.

His puck-handling stands out more than his hockey sense, and he relies more on direct execution than elaborate deception to create chances. Whether he can do that consistently against professional competition remains an open question: He currently has two goals and no assists in 17 KHL games.

Just keep in mind that he's 17 until next May when you read those stats.

3. Philadelphia Flyers: Sergei Skvortsov, LW, Torpedo Nizhny Novgorod (KHL)

Another KHL (and MHL) product is next up on our list, as we have the Philadelphia Flyers drafting Torpedo Nizhny Novgorod and Chaika Nizhny Novgorod winger Sergei Skvortsov.

Unlike Privalov, who has spent the majority of the season with his KHL club, Skvortsov has split the season pretty evenly so far—nine games in the KHL and eight in the MHL at the time of writing—and has a goal and an assist in the KHL, with eight points (three goals, five assists) in the MHL.

Skvortsov is a very different player from Privalov. Where Privalov is heavy power, Skvortsov is slippery dynamism. Why not add another forward of this type to Philadelphia's collection of young players? There, he would join Matvei Michkov, who also scored his first KHL goal before turning 18.

So many of the Flyers' young forwards are complementary players. Don't misunderstand—this is no slight to them, and winning takes all types. But Skvortsov would bring more of the speed, elusiveness, and play-driving ability their forward group needs.

Report Card Grades for Every Team's 1st Month 🔠

4. Los Angeles Kings: Jonah Neuenschwander, C, EHC Biel-Bienne (Swiss NL)

We've hit our first center on the list. There are four more to come.

Swiss forward Jonah Neuenschwander currently plays for EHC Biel-Bienne of the Swiss National League. He's not new to the league, though—he debuted as a 15-year-old, then played 32 games last season at age 16. Professional hockey is something he's used to, and professional hockey is used to him; he's a key part of Biel-Bienne's team at this point. That kind of experience gives a player a certain leg up when it comes to making the transition to North American pro hockey.

So why should the Kings want Neuenschwander? Pro experience isn't enough to draft someone. But you know what is? True two-way ability bolstered by elite hockey sense. Neuenschwander processes the game at a very high level; he's not the manipulative type, but he doesn't need to be to succeed—right now. We'd like to see more of that creativity in playmaking as his game develops further. Regardless, he's trustworthy in just about any situation.

5. Pittsburgh Penguins: Carter Meyer, C, Québec Remparts (QMJHL)

The Pittsburgh Penguins rebuild roller coaster continues, and right now they're in this fifth overall spot in the draft.

Fortunately, there are a plethora of players available who suit the ethos of the rebuild general manager Kyle Dubas and Co. are working toward.

First up, another NTDP product who has moved to different pastures—not the NCAA this time, but the QMJHL.

Carter Meyer is not the first USNTDP player in recent memory to flee the program for a CHL league, and he won't be the last. It's something USA Hockey needs to get a handle on.

For Meyer, his time with the Quebec Remparts is already proving fruitful both in offensive production and in the development needed to prepare him for the big leagues. It also affords him the opportunity to chase a Memorial Cup with his brother, Freddy.

After playing 41 games with the program's U17 team and another 29 with the U18s last season, Meyer has 17 points in 15 games with the Remparts, including five goals. The numbers aren't the main thing to watch, though.

Meyer has good vision, brings speed off the rush and plays hard; consistency is what we'll want to see from him throughout the season.

6. Winnipeg Jets: Milan Sundström, C, Modo Hockey (HockeyAllsvenskan)

For the most part, Swedish center Milan Sundström is currently ranked in the bottom half of the top 10 across the board. Whether that holds remains to be seen, but for the purposes of this mock, it feels logical to have him selected by the Winnipeg Jets.

The Jets are a team whose prospect pool needs to get deeper; the recent waiving of center Brad Lambert underlines the fact that many of their past draft picks haven't panned out as planned.

Sundström brings traits to the table that the Jets will find quite appealing (though someone should remind them that they actually have to develop their prospects, too). Immediate standouts include top-notch hockey sense and phenomenal passing ability.

He's a solid two-way guy, able to process the game at a higher level than many opponents, and playing against seasoned pros will help him sharpen that further.

Sundström has spent time with MoDo Hockey's U20 team and their Allsvenskan team this season, primarily playing with the top club (15 games versus five with the U20s).

7. Columbus Blue Jackets: Alexis Joseph, C, Saint John Sea Dogs (QMJHL)

Saint John Sea Dogs center Alexis Joseph is one of those players who could equally go around the No. 10 range or push into the top three, and there's just no way for us to know which one it's going to be right now.

What we do know is that in this mock, he's available when the Columbus Blue Jackets pick at seventh overall, and he feels like a player who will grab their attention.

Joseph was the first overall pick in his QMJHL draft year, and just about everyone has their eye on him right now thanks to the significant impression he made at last week's QMJHL Top Prospects Game in Gatineau.

His play for Team Lafleur was an excellent microcosm of why any team might want to draft him: scoring goals, directing the flow of play, showcasing physicality, and most importantly, showing scouts that he remembered how to play with pace.

He's dropped a bit on some radars due to concerns about his motor and whether he's going to consistently play with any real urgency; now everyone will be watching to see if he transfers that pace to his regular-season play.

Joseph is currently scoring at a point-per-game pace, with 14 points in 14 games. For a top prospect in his QMJHL draft season, teams will likely want to see more offensive production. But his combination of size and innate skill remains highly appealing if he can make the most of it.

8. Calgary Flames: Brock Cripps, D, Prince Albert Raiders (WHL)

In a brief break from the run of centers, let's look at another defenseman.

The Calgary Flames have made a habit of drafting highly skilled defensemen in recent years. With several of those picks moving into professional hockey or approaching that stage, why not add another to the pipeline?

Prince Albert Raiders defenseman Brock Cripps has the benefit of playing in Calgary's scouting backyard. Though he's undersized at 5'11" and 170 pounds, he handles a substantial workload. He recently logged more than 27 minutes in a game and regularly plays significant minutes, including on both the power play and penalty kill.

He manipulates defenders, moves elusively, and handles the puck exceptionally well. What's not to like? With one goal and 18 assists in 16 games, he's contributing offensively primarily as a facilitator.

Cripps seems like a solid choice for the Flames, especially when you consider no one is getting an immediate gamebreaker at No. 8 this year. Swing for that dynamic right-shot defender.

9. San Jose Sharks: Brock England, C, Seattle Thunderbirds (WHL)

Yes, it's the second player in a row named Brock. It's the WHL. Don't act surprised.

For this mock the method was the best combination of "best player available" and "fits with the current organizational pool," and Brock England is no different.

The Seattle Thunderbirds center stands out first and foremost because of his excellent skating; he's quite fast, and he combines that with an agility that allows him to delay or change direction when needed and has an impressive explosiveness.

With that speed and high-tempo pace being a priority for the Sharks, England feels as though he'll fit right in with the current young corps.

He brings an excellent layer of offense as well, having learned quickly how to use that skating to make opponents' lives miserable. His 21 goals last season were the most goals by a Thunderbirds 16-year-old since Patrick Marleau scored 32 in 1995-96.

Right now he's at 13 points in 14 games; it would not be surprising to see that points pace continue to rise. Things we'll be watching for from him this season include consistency and added physicality.

10. Anaheim Ducks: Dima Zhilkin, RW, Saginaw Spirit (OHL)

The easiest way to explain this pick is that Dima Zhilkin just feels like the rational next step in the Anaheim Ducks' first-round drafting after guys like Nikita Klepov and Roger McQueen.

He's also a really talented player. Zhilkin is a phenomenal point producer, processes the game quickly even under pressure, and plays consistently across all three zones.

You could quibble about his size, but his height doesn't dictate how he plays. He doesn't care that you're bigger; he's going to outwork you and sometimes even push you off pucks. His hockey sense is magnificent, his pace is fantastic, and he's a pain in the butt in an incredibly fun way.

He should be gone before No. 10, and if he plays this way throughout a full season, he very likely will be. He'll certainly rank higher than that on our prospect board. But these mocks let us explore different outcomes, and if the teams picking ahead of Anaheim take other routes, he's a no-brainer for the Ducks.

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 9 2026 NFL Picks
articles.summary: Week 9 in the NFL could be full of upsets.
articles.body:
Week 9 in the NFL could be full of upsets.

The slate features 15 games, including the Cincinnati Bengals' matchup with the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. Of the 14 games that aren't at a neutral site, eight feature home underdogs. Seven road teams are favored by a touchdown or less.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , sniffed out a few trap bets as they navigated through Week 9 games. We'll see how many favorites they faded, and how they approached the bigger spreads.

First, check out our expert standings against the spread. Moton leads the panel midseason, but there's still a long way to go, and trades could change the outlook for some teams.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Nov. 4, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) at Baltimore Ravens (4-4)

I think this line is significantly inflated. Double-digit road wins on Thursdays are extremely rare. The Jaguars are clearly the better team right now, but they're still traveling on short rest to play an experienced, desperate opponent, and they just lost two key defenders to season-ending injuries.

Don't forget they're also without their starting left tackle, Anton Harrison, and Bhayshul Tuten is hurting as well. The Jags might have a major quarterback advantage, but they're far from healthy. This feels like a trap.

Baltimore's quarterback depth was put to the test last weekend, with injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley forcing the Ravens to turn to emergency option Joe Fagnano.

The undrafted rookie may have the benefit of preparing as the starter, but his first start comes against a top-10 scoring defense. The bigger question is whether Baltimore's defense can keep Jacksonville from covering the spread. I'm not counting on it.

Jaguars: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) vs. Atlanta Falcons (3-5)

During his time as Cleveland Browns head coach, Kevin Stefanski regularly got the better of Joe Burrow and the Bengals. I think his experience in those matchups could come into play here, and I have concerns about Cincinnati's ability to corral Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts.

However, I haven't seen enough consistency from Michael Penix Jr. to believe that the Falcons will actually take advantage of a Bengals defense that could come out sluggish in Spain.

The Bengals are the better team, and this is a fairly small line for a neutral-site game.

The Falcons are still drying off from being lost at sea in Tampa Bay—where the Buccaneers floated by on the tide just enough to win a game without completing a single pass.

It was something nobody really needs to watch again. Bijan Robinson and Drake London need to stretch their wings and that means a cover if not an outright win against a Bengals team that inspires very little confidence right now.

Falcons: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell

Denver Broncos (6-2) at Carolina Panthers (3-4)

The Panthers have come back down to earth the past couple of weeks, and the Broncos are flying high after last week's dramatic win over the rival Chiefs. But Denver could be a different team away from Mile High, especially when traveling east to play early. Coming off that big win over Kansas City and with the bye looming, the Broncos will take their foot off the gas just enough for Carolina to cover.

I could see the Panthers' ground game being enough to keep this one close. Denver's defense has looked better in recent weeks, but it still ranks just 23rd in yards per carry allowed. If Chuba Hubbard gets loose, the Broncos could struggle to keep Carolina out of the end zone.

However, I don't believe that firing coordinator Ejiro Evero will instantly give the Panthers a top-tier defense. Carolina's pass defense was atrocious last week in Green Bay, and I think it will allow Bo Nix to build on his best performance of the year.

I expect to see an even matchup early. However, Denver's pass rush will eventually be too much for the Panthers' banged-up offensive line, and the Broncos should pull away late.

Broncos: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Dallas Cowboys (3-5) at Indianapolis Colts (2-6)

The Dallas Cowboys made this writer feel foolish for backing them at home against the Arizona Cardinals. They squandered a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and lost in overtime. Absolutely brutal.

The Cowboys are an untrustworthy team because of their porous defense. If they weren't playing the Indianapolis Colts, who traded two of their best players last week, the opponent would be the side here.

Nonetheless, the Colts are free-falling, and the Cowboys should be able to win by at least a touchdown against a team that's scored 20 or fewer points in three straight games.

Trade speculation surrounding Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor adds another storyline for the Colts this weekend. After he had just eight carries last week, don't expect his workload to increase.

The Colts will almost certainly lean heavily on Seth McGowan and DJ Giddens again, while quarterback Daniel Jones is one or two mistakes from being pulled to see what Anthony Richardson can do. The Dallas Cowboys defense may be bad, but the Colts are coming apart at the seams.

Cowboys: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Cleveland Browns (5-3) at New Orleans Saints (2-5)

I don't really trust either team here, but I'm going with the team that's rested, coming off a bye at home, over the team coming off a loss and on the road again. Both teams have struggled to score this season, but I believe Tyler Shough can do just enough to get New Orleans a win in what will probably be a game that's a race to 20 points. Saints win by a field goal.

The Saints may have had an extra week to prepare for this particular matchup and they're at home, but the Cleveland Browns have a knack for keeping games close, if not finding a way to win outright thanks to a late-game surge.

Plus, the Saints have had issues slowing opposing tight ends this season. Harold Fannin Jr. is arguably the Browns' best player, with 245 receiving yards over the last two weeks. He's going to be a major issue for the Saints to defend, while helping Cleveland's inconsistent offense get on track.

Saints: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton

New York Jets (2-6) at Kansas City Chiefs (5-2)

After back-to-back road losses, the Chiefs return to Arrowhead for what feels like a get-right game. Kansas City has been dominant at home this year. It helps that the Chiefs are playing the Jets, who are in shambles after blowing a multi-score second-half lead to the Raiders at home last week.

Last season, the Jets went 0–3 on the road against teams that entered those games with winning records, losing by an average of 22.7 points. Their last road win over a team with a winning record entering the game came more than four years ago.

I simply don't trust the Chiefs to cover a multi-score spread right now. I'll probably eat those words come next week, but you know what? It was fun watching the Jets game last weekend. I can't believe I just typed that.

Jets: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Detroit Lions (5-2) at Miami Dolphins (1-6)

Miami fights. The Dolphins have only lost one game by more than five points since Week 3. The Lions merely survived despite scoring just 39 points total in back-to-back home wins, but now they're traveling for a potential trap game. A full touchdown is pushing it in this spot.

The Dolphins have covered the spread in four consecutive games. So we must view this team through that lens, but the Lions defense has tightened up with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back on the field in the last two games.

Detroit held the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings to 17 and 15 points, respectively. Playing from behind, the Dolphins may struggle to keep pace with the Lions, who have been a bit stingier on defense lately.

Lions: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

New York Giants (4-2-1) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-6)

So, we're all on the same side, which usually means trouble for that team. Even so, the Philadelphia Eagles offense has struggled mightily, even before the team placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve with blood clots. The Eagles are averaging 14.8 points on their six-game losing streak, and this isn't a get-right game against the NFC East-leading New York Giants coming off a bye week.

I'm hoping for a clean slate with the Giants after their bye week. Every week, they do the opposite of what I write and pick, and while I'm far enough gone in the season to consider the opposite-pick method, I want to believe in this Giants team against a depleted and, simply, not very good Eagles team.

Giants: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Los Angeles Rams (4-4) at Washington Commanders (2-4-1)

There seems to be something of a theme with this week's picks—besides my being wrong. Despite losing wide receiver Terry McLaurin for the season, the Commanders played one of their better offensive games of the campaign last week against the Eagles, and the Rams have covered a spread this big on the road just once this year.

It's getting to the point in the year where the Rams need to start flexing some muscle if they truly have it. Even with all the injuries, this team has more than enough talent and savvy to beat Washington by a touchdown.

Houston Texans (2-5) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-7)

At some point, the Chargers have to look like a competent and competitive football team. I think we'll see it happen this week against a Texans team that has been equally disappointing through the first half of 2026.

Houston's defense has looked nothing like the top-tier unit it was a year ago. While the Texans' pass rush will still present problems for a Chargers offensive line missing Rashawn Slater, a healthier skill group should give Justin Herbert the chance to find a rhythm.

Both teams have struggled, and both will be desperate. The Chargers may not actually pull out the upset, but I think they'll keep it close at home.

Eventually, the Chargers will win a game, right? This weekend's matchup against the Texans may not be their best opportunity. Houston is coming off a bye week after a disappointing start to the season.

Once again, Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has faced significant pressure throughout the campaign. A meeting with Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter won't improve the situation. Besides, Houston had been playing better with back-to-back victories prior to its overtime loss against the New York Giants.

Chargers: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) at San Francisco 49ers (6-1)

Everything logical here is telling me to take the 49ers to win this one going away, and as bad as the Las Vegas defense has been, it's very possible that I'm wrong here.

But this one just feels like a backdoor cover: Kirk Cousins makes a handful of big plays to keep the Raiders in touch, then finds the end zone for a meaningless touchdown to keep a scrappy Las Vegas team within single digits.

The Raiders have allowed 30-plus points in five consecutive games. They just gave up 33 to the New York Jets and fell behind by 11 at halftime last week. Now, they'll face a much tougher opponent coming off a bye week. Also, the San Francisco 49ers may get some banged-up offensive players back for this game.

San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan knows how to script an effective ground attack in many ways, and the Raiders are giving up 5.1 yards per carry, the most in the league. Even if Christian McCaffrey is limited by a hamstring injury, rookie Kaelon Black could have a big day against the Raiders' defensive front while Brock Purdy picks his spots, throwing to George Kittle and Mike Evans (if healthy).

The 49ers bounce back after their sloppy pre-bye-week loss to the Atlanta Falcons.

Raiders: Davenport, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Arizona Cardinals (3-5) at Seattle Seahawks (4-4)

This is simple. We have already seen the Cardinals cover a spread this size on the road against an NFC West opponent. And frankly, the Seahawks are far too inconsistent for me to feel comfortable laying this many points.

The Arizona Cardinals have covered in two of their previous three games, with road wins over the Los Angeles Rams and Dallas Cowboys. So, they should've earned a little more respect than a double-digit line even before the Seahawks ruled out Sam Darnold with a quad injury.

However, the Cardinals will play this game with second-string quarterback Gardner Minshew II and without running back Jeremiyah Love and possibly backup Bam Knight. Arizona's wide receiver corps is also decimated by injuries. Michael Wilson is dealing with broken ribs. Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks are on injured reserve.

Laying double digits is risky given Arizona's recent results, but the Seahawks blew out the Cardinals 31-7 in Arizona in mid-September with backup quarterback Drew Lock, and they can do it again at home.

Seahawks: Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Green Bay Packers (5-3) at New England Patriots (5-3)

My initial estimate on this game was New England by a field goal. If I were getting a hook on the other side of that key number, I'd be on the Packers. It's that simple. The Pats have won all three of their home games by a combined 52 points, while it's been nearly a calendar year since the Packers last won a game by more than a field goal outside of Green Bay.

I have a hard time trusting either team, so I'm backing the underdog in what I expect will be a low-scoring, close game. I think there's the potential for both defenses to dictate this one as both have been strong all season.

In that event, I like Jordan Love and Green Bay's weapons to make a few more important plays than Drake Maye's crew will. The Packers come in on a little extra rest after winning last Thursday and carry that to a narrow win here.

Packers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) at Chicago Bears (6-2)

The Buccaneers have the ingredients to keep this game close: a stingy defense and Bucky Irving's strong recent running. However, I'm not expecting a letdown from Chicago after its dominant win over the Seahawks on Monday.

The addition of Jeffery Simmons should strengthen Chicago's front seven down the stretch. Tampa Bay should improve on last week's passing performance, but I don't expect it to be enough.

The Bears looked like an elite all-around team against the Seahawks in Seattle on Monday night. They'll be back in prime time and back in Chicago for a matchup against a Bucs team that didn't even complete a pass last week.

At first blush, this feels like a massive mismatch. However, I think it's easy to overlook just how good Tampa's defense has been this season. Ben Johnson was able to scheme things up against Seattle, but I think he'll have a harder time here, given Tampa's ability to shut down the run.

The Bucs may not have enough punch in their passing game to actually win this one, especially if Baker Mayfield isn't at 100 percent. However, I think their defense and surging ground game will make this one closer than most expect.

Bears: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Buffalo Bills (6-1) at Minnesota Vikings (6-1)

I'm breaking with my home-underdog theme here. The Vikings will be looking to rebound from last Monday night's loss to Detroit, but I'm concerned their ultra-aggressive defense could backfire against Josh Allen and the Bills.

Allen has been sacked just 13 times this season. Unless Minnesota assigns a defender to shadow him, those blitzes could leave him room to make big plays on the ground.

Despite their record, the Bills are not playing great football. They were frequently out of sync offensively in Baltimore, and the defense was lucky to be facing a third-string quarterback. This is a much more challenging spot for them, especially on the road in prime time. Their three road wins this season have come by a combined 11 points, and they're due for a dud against an absolutely dominant defense.

Bills: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 9 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: With the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans on their byes, fantasy football managers may have relatively few lineup holes to fill. Still, some need a replacement for Lamar Jackson or insurance in case banged-up stars like Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and A.J. Brown are limited or sit out this week.
articles.body:
With the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans on their byes, fantasy football managers may have relatively few lineup holes to fill. Still, some need a replacement for Lamar Jackson or insurance in case banged-up stars like Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and A.J. Brown are limited or sit out this week.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Jackson will likely miss the rest of the season after undergoing thumb surgery. So, if you don't have a viable backup quarterback on your bench, choose wisely from the free-agent pool. Two young signal-callers are worth considering for the long term.

Two rookie running backs are working their way into consistent roles with solid production in recent weeks; one could see an uptick in touches because of a star ball-carrier's "mild" injury.

An undersized slot receiver could be a safe WR2 with upside as a lead pass-catcher in a favorable matchup.

Lastly, two underrated tight ends are on the cusp of becoming must-roster players, and they're both widely available.

Here are eight sleepers for Week 9—all available in at least 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros' roster consensus percentages.

QB Malik Willis vs. Detroit Lions (23 Percent Rostered)

Malik Willis has thrown for two touchdowns twice this season, both instances following the Miami Dolphins' Week 6 bye. Over the last two weeks, he's finished as QB4 and QB15 in matchups against the New York Jets and the New England Patriots.

Willis could post a solid stat line for the third straight week against the Detroit Lions, who allow the most fantasy points to quarterbacks. The Lions defense has been stingier lately, but it's allowed at least two passing touchdowns in every game this season.

Furthermore, the Lions will be without the quarterback of their defense, 2025 first-team All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell, who suffered a scary neck injury last week. Willis could see some opportunities to attack the middle of the field in the passing game and run when his receivers aren't open.

Even if the Lions blow out the Dolphins, Willis can rack up fantasy points in garbage time, giving him a high production floor this week.

QB Michael Penix Jr. vs. Cincinnati Bengals (21 Percent Rostered)

After throwing for three touchdowns in three straight outings, Michael Penix Jr. had a dud in a rainy game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week. He'll face the Cincinnati Bengals' 26th-ranked pass defense in Madrid at Estadio Santiago Bernabéu, a venue with a retractable roof.

Although the Bengals have allowed only eight passing touchdowns in seven games, they've given up 304 passing yards to Cam Ward and 298 to Tyler Huntley in their previous two outings.

Penix poses a bigger passing threat than the aforementioned quarterbacks and should bounce back after throwing four interceptions last week.

FanDuel has an over/under total of 52.5 points for this game, so it could be an entertaining high-scoring battle. If so, Penix could be primed for another multi-touchdown passing performance.

RB Kaelon Black vs. Las Vegas Raiders (25 Percent Rostered)

According to San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan , running back Christian McCaffrey suffered a "mild" hamstring strain in Week 7.

If Kaelon Black is available in your league, it's a good time to pick him up. He played 47 percent of the 49ers' offensive snaps in his previous outing, the most of any game this season.

Though McCaffrey has a good chance to suit up this week, the 49ers could limit his snaps to preserve him for the season. He may split carries almost evenly with Black, as we've seen a few times this year.

In Week 7, Black logged 12 rush attempts for 63 yards and a touchdown. If the rookie tailback gets double-digit carries, he has high-end flex appeal and RB2 upside in a matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders' 31st-ranked run defense.

The Raiders just gave up 147 yards and a touchdown to the New York Jets' second-string running back Braelon Allen, and they have allowed at least 103 rushing yards in all but one game this season.

Black could have a career day if the 49ers ease up significantly on McCaffrey's workload.

RB Emmett Johnson vs. New York Jets (21 Percent Rostered)

The Kansas City Chiefs need explosive plays, and Emmett Johnson delivered as a receiver last week, catching five passes for 128 yards and a touchdown against the Denver Broncos.

In Week 8, Johnson's 73-yard touchdown catch inflated his receiving totals, but his five targets represented a healthy workload for an RB2. The rookie fifth-rounder's pass-catching isn't just a one-off flash; he's caught 14 passes for 237 yards, along with last week's touchdown.

The New York Jets field the 21st-ranked run defense and have allowed 131 or more rushing yards in four of their last six games. If Kenneth Walker III gets most of the touches on the ground, Johnson can still catch a few passes to put up a solid stat line.

Last week, the Las Vegas Raiders relegated running back Ashton Jeanty to a receiving role, and he caught three passes for 64 yards against the Jets. Johnson is in a good spot to be productive while spelling Walker on the ground and coming in on obvious passing downs.

WR DeMario Douglas vs. Green Bay Packers (31 Percent Rostered)

Last week, New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown logged a limited practice session on Wednesday and sat out Thursday and Friday with ankle and knee injuries . The team ruled him out for Week 8. Brown hasn't returned to practice.

Given Brown's recent absences, fantasy managers should roster wide receivers DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism III. Also, keep an eye on Mack Hollins, who logged a full practice Wednesday after missing a month with a calf injury. That said, Douglas is the preferred sleeper option because of his steady role in the Patriots offense over the last few weeks.

Douglas has racked up at least 65 receiving yards in three of the previous four games and scored four touchdowns in that stretch. In last week's win over the Miami Dolphins, he led the Patriots with 76 receiving yards.

The Green Bay Packers are tied for 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers, so Douglas is a solid flex play regardless of Brown's status, though he would be a decent WR2 if the star receiver is out for consecutive weeks.

WR Malachi Fields at Philadelphia Eagles (9 Percent Rostered)

Dig deep into your league's free-agent pool and add Malachi Fields. He's shown signs of development in the New York Giants' passing attack, with third-string quarterback J.J. McCarthy under center.

In Week 6, Fields played a season-high 93.5 percent of offensive snaps, but he caught only two of his eight targets for 19 yards. In the following week, the rookie third-rounder had a more efficient outing, catching four of his five targets for 83 yards.

McCarthy's rapport with Fields is still a work in progress, but their connection showed clear signs of growth before the New York Giants' Week 8 bye.

Now, the Giants face the Philadelphia Eagles, who allow the most fantasy points to wide receivers. That bodes well for Malik Nabers, but if Fields sees a handful of targets, he could feast too. Also, at 6'4", 222 pounds, the big-bodied receiver is a viable red-zone threat.

TE Mike Gesicki vs. Atlanta Falcons, in Madrid (21 Percent Rostered)

Mike Gesicki has scored a touchdown in six of seven games this season and takes a five-game scoring streak to Madrid in a decent matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Even if Gesicki doesn't reach paydirt, he could rack up strong receiving numbers as a complement to wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

The Falcons allowed at least 59 receiving yards to a tight end in three of their last five games. In Week 5, they gave up 54 receiving yards to Baltimore Ravens tight ends Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas combined.

As the Bengals' primary pass-catching tight end, Gesicki has a good chance to top 50 receiving yards and extend his touchdown streak.

TE Greg Dulcich vs. Detroit Lions (7 Percent Rostered)

This past offseason, Greg Dulcich generated buzz as one of Malik Willis' primary targets. After a slow start, he's picked up momentum, with his production rising over the last few weeks.

Dulcich has at least four receptions in three straight games, logging 13 catches for 166 yards in that stretch. He's second on the team in receptions (22) and receiving yards (256).

This week, Dulcich will face the Detroit Lions, who have allowed the most fantasy points to tight ends and are without starting three-down linebacker Jack Campbell.

FanDuel has set the over/under at 50.5 points for this game. If the Miami Dolphins keep pace with the Lions, Willis will have to accumulate yards through the air, and Dulcich could be his primary or secondary target.

Fantasy points scored against statistics are provided by FantasyPros .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: What to watch as the NFL season crosses the halfway point
articles.summary: We’ve crossed the halfway point of the NFL season, and the race to separate contenders from pretenders is heating up.
articles.body: We’ve crossed the halfway point of the NFL season, and the race to separate contenders from pretenders is heating up. From Joe Burrow taking his hot streak to Spain to Josh Allen facing Minnesota’s stingy defense, here are five things to know for Week 9. Burrow brings the fireworks to Spain We turned the clocks back last Sunday and gained an extra hour of sleep. Wouldn’t that have been the perfect morning for an international NFL game? West Coast fans, especially, could have used the assist. Instead, the overseas action returns this Sunday, with the Cincinnati Bengals facing the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. The Estadio Santiago Bernabéu will host its second regular-season NFL game after the Miami Dolphins beat the Washington Commanders 16-13 in overtime there last November. International games don’t always deliver marquee offenses, but Spanish fans should get a good look at one of the league’s hottest quarterbacks. Joe Burrow has thrown 13 touchdown passes during Cincinnati’s three-game winning streak, pushing himself into the MVP conversation. Atlanta, meanwhile, could use a fresh start – and a dry football – after being shut out in a rain-soaked loss at Tampa Bay. The Falcons should find more opportunities against a Bengals defense that just surrendered 36 points to Tennessee. With Burrow rolling and Cincinnati still struggling to get stops, this one has the ingredients for an entertaining morning. Kickoff is at 9:30 a.m. ET. Can the Cowboys get out of their own way? Being a Dallas Cowboys fan is tough. Just when Philadelphia’s injuries appeared to give Dallas an opening in the NFC East, the Cowboys found another painful way to lose. They led Arizona 24-10 with about 11 minutes remaining Sunday, only to unravel in a 33-30 overtime defeat. Even a second chance wasn’t enough. Chad Ryland missed an extra point that would have put the Cardinals ahead with six seconds left in regulation, but Dak Prescott and the Cowboys still couldn’t turn that reprieve into a victory. Dallas entered the game 69-0 when leading at home by at least 14 points in the fourth quarter. There goes that perfect record. Afterward, owner Jerry Jones defended head coach Brian Schottenheimer, saying others had let the coach down. Wherever the blame lands, the Cowboys are 3-5 and running out of room for these kinds of mistakes. The good news? The NFC East remains within reach, and Dallas’ next four games are against the Colts, 49ers, Titans and Eagles. Winning three would get the Cowboys back to .500 at 6-6. That’s an attainable goal. With this team, though, nothing feels guaranteed. Minshew Mania is back Minshew Magic is back! As Adam Rank put it on X: “Gardner Minshew is like the McRib. He exists for just a limited amount of time. But while he’s here, it’s spectacular.” The veteran quarterback came off Arizona’s bench late in the third quarter Sunday and promptly turned a forgettable afternoon into one of the season’s wildest comebacks. Minshew threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns, rallying the Cardinals past the Cowboys in overtime. His reward? Head coach Mike LaFleur named him the starter moving forward. Minshew has been delivering these moments since his rookie season with Jacksonville in 2019, when he threw 21 touchdown passes against just six interceptions. The signature mustache, aviator sunglasses and occasional late-game magic have helped make him a fan favorite wherever he lands. The Cardinals will be the sixth team for which Minshew has started. But can he turn another memorable cameo into a sustained run? His first assignment is a tough one: A trip to Seattle, where the Seahawks will be eager to respond after giving up 34 points to Chicago on Monday night. Baker and Bucs at the Bears On Sunday, the Buccaneers pulled off the unthinkable: Winning an NFL game without completing a pass. With rain pouring down in Tampa, the Bucs leaned on their running game and bulldozed Atlanta for a franchise-record 324 rushing yards in a 16-0 victory. They became the first NFL team to win without a completion since the Buffalo Bills in 1974. Baker Mayfield finished 0-for-3 and somehow still posted a higher passer rating than Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who threw four interceptions. Tampa Bay will almost certainly need more from its passing game Sunday night in Chicago. The Bears looked like legitimate Super Bowl contenders in their 34-17 win over Seattle on Monday, handing the Seahawks their first loss by multiple scores since 2024. Chicago’s 6-2 record is its best eight-game start in 14 years, and Ben Johnson’s offense is thriving. In the four games Caleb Williams has started and finished this season, the Bears have scored 59, 30, 31 and 34 points. Josh Allen vs. the Vikings’ defense Monday night brings a clash of styles — and a fascinating test for two contenders. Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills arrive in Minnesota averaging a league-best 33 points per game. Brian Flores and the Vikings’ defense are allowing a league-low 13. Something has to give. Both teams enter at 6-1, with Minnesota looking to bounce back after Detroit handed the Vikings their first loss of the season. The matchup to watch is Allen against Flores’ pressure packages. Can the Vikings disguise their looks, get home with the blitz and force mistakes? Or will Allen escape the rush and punish Minnesota with the kind of big plays that can wreck even the best defensive game plan? It’s a terrific chess match to close the week – with two teams hoping it’s a preview of much bigger games to come.

articles.title: Travis Kelce and BLACKPINK's Jisoo join forces with global sports and entertainment stars for Tommy Hilfiger
articles.summary: Travis Kelce is adding another fashion moment to an already eventful year.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is adding another fashion moment to an already eventful year. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has joined an impressive lineup of global stars for Tommy Hilfiger's winter 2026 campaign, which puts a personal spin on holiday celebrations. Alongside K-pop sensation Jisoo, NBA player Josh Hart and several football stars, Kelce appears in a campaign built around family traditions, festive rituals and individual style. However, it is his first holiday season as a married man that gives his appearance a particularly personal touch.Travis Kelce shares first holiday plans as a married manKelce's appearance in the Tommy Hilfiger campaign comes after a major personal milestone. The NFL star married Taylor Swift during the summer of 2026, making this holiday season a new experience for the couple.Speaking about the celebrations, Kelce revealed his excitement about starting a fresh chapter while holding on to familiar traditions.“I’m excited for my first holiday as a married man,” said Kelce, who married Taylor Swift this past summer. “I love all the old traditions and can’t wait to start some new ones. I start celebrating as that tree goes up,” said Kelce, the tight end for the Kansas City Chiefs.His comments offer a glimpse into the festive atmosphere he enjoys away from football. The campaign also shows how the holiday season can mean something different to everyone, whether it involves family gatherings, food or simply spending time at home.Kelce wears a wool chore jacket from the winter collection, bringing a relaxed yet polished look to the campaign.Jisoo, Josh Hart and other stars join Tommy Hilfiger's winter campaignTommy Hilfiger's winter 2026 campaign brings together an international group of athletes, entertainers and digital creators. Alongside Kelce and Jisoo, the lineup includes actor Arón Piper, creator Quen Blackwell, New York Knicks star Josh Hart and Liverpool FC players Florian Wirtz, Dominik Szoboszlai and Jérémy Jacquet.Each personality shares a different holiday tradition. Piper enjoys winter swimming in northern Spain, while Wirtz competes with his sister over music selections. Blackwell takes festive decorations further with a drone light show. Hart, meanwhile, has a special appreciation for curry goat.Jisoo also shared her idea of a perfect holiday, which involves plenty of rest and good food.“My perfect holiday is all about taking it easy,” said Jisoo, the South Korean singer, songwriter and actress who rose to global fame as a member of the K-pop girl group Blackpink. “If it’s a day off, I’ll sleep as long as I can and hopefully wake up around dinner time. Then I’ll order something delicious with dessert arriving at the same time so I can go straight from one to the other. That’s my idea of a very good day.”Tommy Hilfiger said the campaign celebrates individuality, family connections and the personalities behind familiar public figures.Shot by Edward Cooke, the campaign will roll out through weekly video releases ahead of the holidays.
