articles.title: NFL Trade Rumors, Predictions for Derrick Henry, Brian Thomas Jr. and Jessie Bates III
articles.summary: The NFL trade market is active.
articles.body:
And there's a pretty good chance the activity only increases as the football world moves closer to Tuesday's trade deadline.

The Baltimore Ravens were the latest squad to enter the roster-strengthening game, as they addressed their injury-riddled quarterback room with veteran Jacoby Brissett. Bigger splashes have already been made (Quenton Nelson, Jeffery Simmons and DeForest Buckner), but it's always notable when a signal-caller relocates.

What might the football gods cook up next? Let's lean on the latest rumor mill chatter to find out.

The Atlanta Falcons have a playoff pulse. It stems almost exclusively from the fact they reside in the AFC South, where no one has a winning record and the division owns a collective 11-19 mark.

While Atlanta could escape this division, it should have a healthy amount of skepticism about its ability to go on any kind of deep postseason run. Selective selling could be in the cards, then, and if it is, it's possible—though apparently not probable—that playmaking safety Jessie Bates III could be on the move.

"I do not believe the Faclons are trying to trade Bates, and I would be surprised if they did," ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote. "But he's an excellent player in the final year of his contract, and there are teams out there that would like to know whether they can get him."

The Falcons owe it to themselves (and their future) to at least have an ear open to hear what the market might be willing to give up to get Bates. In the end, though, it probably won't be enough for them to actually sign off on a swap.

If Jacoby Brissett can't stabilize the Ravens—and he was benched in his most recent game with the Arizona Cardinals—then Baltimore, which enters Thursday night amid a three-game losing streak, could look toward its future and consider shipping out present contributors for long-term assets.

Might that mean splitting from bellcow running back Derrick Henry? It seems like there's at least a universe in which that's the case.

"As running back names swirl, keep half an eye on Baltimore's Derrick Henry," Graziano wrote. "... Henry is turning 33 in January. He is scheduled to earn $12 million next year, and none of that money is guaranteed. If he isn't in Baltimore's plans beyond this year, the Ravens could find themselves fielding offers over the next week."

Henry has been incredible across two-plus seasons in Baltimore (4,148 rushing yards, 43 touchdowns in 42 games), and he could be incredibly valuable to a running back-needy shopper. A trade feels like a longshot, but that could depend on the Ravens' confidence in Brissett to hold things over until whenever Lamar Jackson is ready to return.

Teams Hoping To Pry Brian Thomas Jr. Out of Jacksonville?

It's been a strange NFL journey so far for receiver Brian Thomas Jr. He joined the Jacksonville Jaguars as the 23rd pick in the 2024 NFL draft, earned Pro Bowl honors as a rookie for his 1,330-scrimmage yard, 10-touchdown debut and then has backtracked down the pecking order ever since.

That's had people talking about his future and whether it should still exist in Jacksonville. As ESPN's Ian Rapoport noted, though, those talks aren't necessarily happening within the Jaguars' organization.

"Brian Thomas Jr. has been the area of interest for a lot of other teams," Rapoport said. "... What we don't know is would Jacksonville actually move him. They're a good team, he had a touchdown last week. He is getting more and more reps as we've kind of gone on this season. Woud they actually move on from him knowing what is out there for them? Time will tell."

It'll take a good offer to get Thomas, but it feels entirely plausible that one comes across the table. Between his past production and long-term potential, plus the number of contenders with needs at the position, there are a lot of arrows pointing toward a deal getting done.

Prediction: Thomas is traded to the Kansas City Chiefs.

articles.title: Jacoby Brissett Reportedly Restructures Contract Ahead of Ravens Trade, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Ahead of his rumored trade to the Baltimore Ravens, the Arizona Cardinals reportedly restructured quarterback Jacoby Brissett's contract on Thursday.
articles.body:
Ahead of his rumored trade to the Baltimore Ravens, the Arizona Cardinals reportedly restructured quarterback Jacoby Brissett's contract on Thursday.

According to ESPN's Field Yates , $2.7 million of Brissett's remaining $5.4 million salary this season was converted into a signing bonus, meaning the Ravens will owe him $2.7 million if the trade is completed today or $2.43 million if the trade is completed after that.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Wednesday that the Ravens were finalizing a trade for Brissett, although it is not expected to become official until this coming weekend.

Baltimore's reported acquisition of Brissett comes amid a rash of injuries at the quarterback position for the Ravens.

After missing three games with an ankle injury, Lamar Jackson returned to start against the Buffalo Bills this past weekend, but on the Ravens' first offensive play from scrimmage, he suffered a thumb injury and was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

The injury required surgery and a trip to injured reserve. Head coach Jesse Minter admitted that the injury could "potentially" be season-ending.

On top of that, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley suffered a turf toe injury against the Bills, and he has been ruled out for the remainder of the season.

Baltimore turned to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano under center with both Jackson and Huntley out, and he largely struggled in a 36-10 loss to the Bills.

Despite that, Fagnano will get his first career start on Thursday night when the Ravens host the Jacksonville Jaguars.

However, assuming the Brissett trade gets completed in the coming days, he figures to take on the starting role in Baltimore until and unless Jackson is able to return.

Brissett, 33, is an 11-year NFL veteran who has played for six different teams over the course of his career.

He has spent the past two seasons in Arizona, starting 20 of the 22 games he appeared in for the Cards.

Although Brissett went just 1-11 as the starter last season, he largely played well, completing 64.9 percent of his passes for 3,366 yards, 23 touchdowns and eight interceptions.

In eight starts this season, Brissett is 3-5, while completing 63.3 percent of his passing attempts for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven picks.

Brissett was pulled during the Cardinals' game against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, though, and Gardner Minshew threw three touchdown passes in the third quarter, as Arizona came from behind to beat Dallas 33-30 in overtime.

As a result of his performance, Minshew was named the new starter, while Brissett was dropped to third on the depth chart behind rookie Carson Beck.

The writing was on the wall for Brissett in Arizona at that point, but Baltimore offers an exciting, new opportunity, as the Ravens are still very much in the AFC playoff race with a record of 4-4.

articles.title: “He's a guy that I love dearly”: How Josh Allen repaid Brian Daboll's support after Buffalo Bills coach lost the grandmother who raised him
articles.summary: Josh Allen knew the pain Brian Daboll was going through.
articles.body: Josh Allen knew the pain Brian Daboll was going through. The Buffalo Bills quarterback had once broken down in his coach's arms after losing his own grandmother. Nearly a year later, Daboll faced the same heartbreak. He had lost the woman who raised him, and Allen did not let the difficult week pass without acknowledging what his coach meant to him. After Buffalo's win over Washington, the quarterback dedicated the performance to Daboll.It was an emotional role reversal for the two men. In November 2020, Daboll had been there to comfort Allen. On September 26, 2021, Allen returned that support with a heartfelt tribute that showed just how close their relationship had become. How Brian Daboll comforted Josh Allen after his grandmother's deathAllen's loss came on November 7, 2020, when his grandmother, Patricia Allen, died unexpectedly at 80. The news arrived on the eve of Buffalo's game against the Seattle Seahawks. Despite the heartbreak, Allen decided to play.He later explained that one thought kept him going. His grandmother would have wanted him to be on the field, enjoying the game he loved."All I kept telling myself was she would've wanted me to play," Allen told reporters on November 11, 2020, while discussing his grandmother's death and the Seahawks game.The quarterback honoured that thought with a remarkable performance. Buffalo beat Seattle 44-34 on November 8, with Allen completing 31 of 38 passes for 415 yards and four total touchdowns.But once the game ended, the emotions caught up with him. Allen entered the locker room and broke down. Daboll, then the Bills' offensive coordinator, was there to hold him.Daboll recalled the moment while speaking to reporters on November 9, 2020."When he came in off the field and into the locker room, he kind of fell into my arms a little bit," he said.The coach also spoke about how difficult it was to watch someone he cared about deal with such a painful loss. For Allen, that embrace came at a moment when he needed it most. How Josh Allen returned the favour after Daboll lost the woman who raised himLess than a year later, Daboll faced a similar loss. His grandmother, the woman who raised him, died just days before Buffalo's September 26, 2021, game against Washington.Allen knew that his coach was going through a difficult time. He also remembered how Daboll had stood beside him after Patricia's death. This time, the quarterback wanted to give something back.The Bills responded with a 43-21 win over Washington. Allen threw for 358 yards and four touchdowns, but his words after the game carried a much more personal message.During his postgame press conference on September 26, 2021, Allen spoke about Daboll's loss."He lost his grandma this week, the woman who raised him," Allen said.He then brought up the moment from the previous season when Daboll had caught him in the locker room."It's just crazy how the roles are reversed. Ya know, last year I got to come in the locker room and have a heartfelt hug with him, and this year, he falls into my arms. He's a guy that I love dearly," Allen said.The quarterback also explained that the players understood what Daboll and his family were facing. They wanted to execute well and give their coach a performance he could appreciate during such a difficult week.Allen was not alone in paying tribute. Offensive lineman Dion Dawkins also dedicated the victory to Daboll, while head coach Sean McDermott praised the togetherness within the team.For Allen, the win was about more than putting another victory on Buffalo's record. Daboll had caught him during one of the lowest moments of his life. When the coach experienced his own heartbreak, Allen made sure he was there for him. Nearly a year apart, those two locker-room moments showed how much their bond meant to both men.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Robert Kraft to Miss Rob Gronkowski's Patriots HOF Induction After Having Back Surgery
articles.summary: New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft will miss former tight end and franchise legend Rob Gronkowski's induction into the team's Hall of Fame on Saturday as he recovers from back surgery, he told ESPN's Mike Reiss.
articles.body:
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft will miss former tight end and franchise legend Rob Gronkowski's induction into the team's Hall of Fame on Saturday as he recovers from back surgery, he told ESPN's Mike Reiss .

"As much pain as I was in before having surgery, it pains me even more to miss the ceremony," Kraft said.

Kraft told Reiss the injury will keep him on "injured reserve." He said doctors told him to stay off his feet, so he won't be at the team's next two games: a home contest vs. the Green Bay Packers on Sunday and a neutral-site matchup against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Nov. 15 in Munich, Germany.

Gronkowski is one of the greatest tight ends in NFL history, and he'll be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame shortly, perhaps as soon as 2027, when he's first eligible for induction.

Gronkowski played nine seasons with the Pats (2010-2018) and two more with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2020-2021). During his time with New England, Gronkowski won three Super Bowls (2014, 2016 and 2018 seasons) and also made five Pro Bowls and four All-Pro First Teams.

He finished top five in the Associated Press Offensive Player of the Year race twice and won the AP's Comeback Player of the Year award in 2014 after being held to six games in 2013 .

Gronkowski also won his fourth and final Super Bowl with the 2020 Bucs.

The former University of Arizona star persevered despite dealing with a litany of injuries. He also underwent three back surgeries dating back to his time with the Wildcats.

"I always told Gronk that in my next life, I wanted to come back as him because I had never seen him have a bad day," Kraft told Reiss. "But after a couple of back surgeries, I take that back. I never want to experience that again."

According to Reiss, fans voted Gronkowski into the team's Hall of Fame back in April during his first year of eligibility.

These days, Gronkowski is a full-time studio analyst on Fox NFL Sunday and Fox NFL Kickoff. According to Reiss, Kraft wanted to induct Gronkowski into the Hall of Fame earlier this season.

However, the only Pats home game airing on Fox this year is this Sunday, when Fox is also committed to its annual Salute to Service coverage in advance of Veterans Day.

Ultimately, the induction will take place Saturday.

Gronkowski will have a busy Sunday, as he'll be part of Fox's pregame Salute to Service coverage, which will broadcast simultaneously from the United States Military Academy at West Point in New York and the United States Naval Academy (Annapolis) in Maryland.

Kickoff in Foxborough, Massachusetts, is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Robert Kraft to miss Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame induction while recovering from back surgery
articles.summary: Gronkowski signed a one-day contract last year to retire as a Patriot.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots will induct Rob Gronkowski into the team's Hall of Fame on Saturday, but one important person will not be in attendance.

Patriots owner Robert Kraft recently underwent back surgery and is "on injured reserve," forcing him to miss the festivities. The 85-year-old told ESPN's Mike Reiss that doctors have told him to stay off his feet while he recovers, which will also keep him away from the team's upcoming game on Sunday in Foxborough against the Green Bay Packers and in Week 10 when they take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.

"As much pain as I was in before having surgery, it pains me even more to miss the ceremony," Kraft said .

Last November, Gronkowski signed a one-day contract with the Patriots, allowing him to retire with the franchise he helped win three Super Bowls in nine NFL seasons. Five months later, he was voted into the Patriots' Hall of Fame as its 38th inductee.

The longtime tight end was a second-round draft pick by the Patriots in 2010 and finished his career as the franchise's leader in total touchdowns (80) and is second in receiving yards with 7,861.

Gronkowski played nine of his 11 NFL seasons in New England and was a four-time first-team All-Pro, five-time Pro Bowler, and a member of the 2010s All-Decade Team and NFL 100th Anniversary Team.

Gronkowski is eligible for induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2027.

articles.title: Vikings Reportedly 'Trending Towards' QB1 Change vs. Bills amid Kyler Murray's Hamstring Injury
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings will likely have a new quarterback at the helm for Monday's game against the Buffalo Bills, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings will likely have a new quarterback at the helm for Monday's game against the Buffalo Bills, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Schefter said on Get Up that "it is trending towards" Carson Wentz taking over for Kyler Murray, who's nursing a hamstring issue:

The injury could provide a handy reason for Minnesota to make a switch some fans will argue is justified anyway.

Signing Murray to a one-year contract made sense given the paltry cost . The move simply isn't working out.

Since returning from a concussion in Week 3, the two-time Pro Bowler has thrown for 1,004 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions in five starts. He ranks 26th among qualified players in QBR (44.7) at ESPN.com .

It's getting more and more difficult to maintain hope that Murray can be a successful reclamation project in the vein of Sam Darnold or Baker Mayfield.

Wentz threw for three touchdowns after filling in for Murray in a 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers, but it was a much different story when he started in Week 2. He went 11-of-20 for 143 yards as Minnesota lost 9-3 to the Chicago Bears.

The fact some would posit the 33-year-old is an upgrade over Murray speaks to how poorly Murray is performing. Wentz is a better pure passer, and that might be enough to make a meaningful difference for the offense.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's Potential Trade Timeline Updated in New NFL Rumors amid Colts' Fire Sale
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have reportedly taken "plenty of calls" on several players, including three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor, amid their fire sale, but the current plan is to wait until after their home game against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday to make any determination about potential deals.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have reportedly taken "plenty of calls" on several players, including three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor, amid their fire sale, but the current plan is to wait until after their home game against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday to make any determination about potential deals.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, that means the fates of Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs and defensive tackle Grover Stewart will be decided sometime early next week:

The 2-6 Colts have already traded left guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round pick.

The Colts have already parted ways with general manager Chris Ballard, ending his tenure after nine seasons. Assistant GM Ed Dodds has taken over on an interim basis.

The rebuild is on in Indianapolis, which is playing out the string at this point. The Colts have lost four straight games, capped by a 42-7 road loss to the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars last week.

At this point, it hard to believe that Taylor will be around much longer, although the Colts are apparently holding out hopes for a massive deal.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that they are hoping for a "Christian McCaffrey" return, referencing when the Carolina Panthers traded the star running back to the San Francisco 49ers in 2022 for four picks (2023 second, third and fourth-rounders and a 2024 fifth-rounder).

The four-time 1,000-yard rusher and two-time league touchdown leader has amassed 812 yards from scrimmage and eight touchdowns in eight games in his seventh NFL season.

ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that the Denver Broncos, New York Giants, Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers have interest in Taylor.

Wide receiver Josh Downs, who has already requested a trade, is in the final year of his rookie contract and would certainly appear on his way out at this point. Downs has 30 catches for 330 yards and a touchdown through eight games. He had career-highs of 72 receptions for 803 yards and five TD in 2024.

Stewart is in his 10th season (all with the Colts). He has 26 tackles, three quarterback hits and a half-sack in eight games. Stewart is in the final season of his three-year, $39 million contract .

"Stewart might be a little tougher to deal, since his base salary this year is $11.74 million, so an acquiring team would need to be able to fit about half that under its salary cap," ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote. But there are enough teams looking for interior linemen that he likely finds a new home at some point in the next week."

Ultimately, multiple Colts are likely playing their last games in Indianapolis on Sunday, when they host Dallas at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jaguars favored by 10 over Ravens as Lamar Jackson injury looms large
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence's 17 touchdowns and four interceptions lead the 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars into a matchup against a Ravens team missing Lamar Jackson.
articles.body: We are officially at the halfway mark of the regular season for the NFL. Once this week’s games are over, 50% of the season is done, and we should have a pretty good idea of who will make the postseason and who will not. You can always look at the standings to see playoff projections, but it is a fun time to reevaluate the teams. The Jacksonville Jaguars are likely to make the postseason, but the Baltimore Ravens are unlikely. The Jaguars are one of the better teams in the AFC, and currently sit at 5-2 for the season. They are just 1-1 for the season on the road, which means they have a lot of road games remaining. That could be a bit of an issue for the team. Their wins have been over the Browns, Patriots, Bengals, Eagles, and Colts. None of those teams are overly impressive this season, but I also don’t think any of them were terrible. Their two losses this season have come against the Texans (by three points) and to the Broncos on the road. In fairness to the Jaguars, the loss to the Texans came in a different country. But that was the second straight week in London. I am not a big Trevor Lawrence guy, but I have to say that he has been fantastic this year. He has 17 touchdown passes and four interceptions to go along with almost 1700 passing yards. It is possible this will be his best statistical season of his career. RAVENS TURN TO UNDRAFTED ROOKIE JOE FAGNANO AFTER LAMAR JACKSON LANDS ON IR, COACH JESSIE MINTER SAYS The Ravens come into this game with a 4-4 record and a 1-2 mark in Baltimore. I suppose you can blame this season on a wide variety of things, but the main issue for the Ravens is Lamar Jackson not being available. Last week, Jackson dropped back to pass and was injured on the first offensive snap. He continues to be a dynamic playmaker, but he gets injured all the time. To make matters worse, they lost their backup quarterback only a few drives later. Derrick Henry has been (and is) great, but even he can’t really run when the box is completely loaded against him. The Jaguars are already good against the run, so knowing that they are facing a backup or third-string quarterback, the Ravens should expect to have to throw to win this game. They will clearly need help from the defense. The Ravens are a bottom-half team against the pass, but slightly better against the run. Baltimore is also allowing 25.4 points per game to opponents. However, their rush defense has been fantastic, and they are only allowing 15.9 points per game. The points per game numbers are heavily influenced by the wins over the Browns and Colts, though. It is hard to see a path where the Ravens succeed. When Joe Fagnano took over last week, he got them 91 yards and one interception. The only touchdown came from Henry after they intercepted the ball in the red zone. I think the Jaguars will cover the -10. It probably will be sweaty, but I just don’t see how Fagnano improves enough in a short week to give them the cover. articles.title: Saints look to reverse an ugly history against the Browns this Sunday
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints must step up and get a win against the Cleveland Browns in Week 9. Here's a look at series history between the two teams.
articles.body:
After a Week 8 bye, the New Orleans Saints return to action on Sunday when they host the Cleveland Browns . The Saints stumble in with a 2-5 record but still very much in the NFC South race. Cleveland enters with a surprising 5-3 mark, playing their third consecutive game on the road. This will be only the 21st meeting between the Saints and Browns franchise. Here's a look at who holds the edge in the series between the teams.

Last meeting: 2024 in New Orleans (Saints 35-14)

These teams were actually division opponents for one year in 1968, the second year of existence for New Orleans. It was in the NFL Century Division, two years before the AFL-NFL merger. Cleveland dominated this short series at the beginning. The Browns won the first eight times these teams faced, with five of those matchups in New Orleans.

The Saints finally broke their eight-game losing streak against the Browns in 1984 with a 16-14 triumph in Cleveland. The Saints followed that up three years later with a 28-21 win over the Browns in the Superdome. It was their first home win against Cleveland and the second of three straight wins over the Browns, their longest such streak. Since Cleveland rattled those eight consecutive wins to start this series, New Orleans actually has a 7-5 edge over the Browns but are a rather mediocre 4-4 against Cleveland all-time inside the Superdome.

New Orleans has won their last three matchups against the Browns, equaling their longest streak. Two of those games have been at home. The second of which was a 35-14 victory in 2024, the last time these teams met. It was both the largest margin of victory for the Saints against the Browns and the only time they'd scored over 30 points against them in 20 meetings.

Prior to this season, the Saints and Browns have met four times in November. Cleveland has won three of those games, with the only exception being that resounding New Orleans victory on November 17, 2024 in the last matchup between the two. The Saints hope to have that same fortune again this time around. New Orleans has yet to win a game in the Superdome this season, losing three straight at home between weeks 4-6. If the Saints have any hope of staying in the horrible NFC South race, they need to immediately reverse that trend against the Browns on Sunday.

articles.title: Knicks' Mike Brown makes stance on ex-Laker Dalton Knecht crystal clear after debut vs. Bulls
articles.summary: Dalton Knecht made his New York Knicks debut on Wednesday night and it was pretty solid. After the game, head coach Mike Brown made it obvious what he thinks...
articles.body:
This season has already been a rollercoaster for former Los Angeles Lakers first-round pick Dalton Knecht, and it hasn't been long at all. Knecht was once considered the steal of the 2024 NBA Draft by Los Angeles.

However, things have not gone according to plan after he saw limited playing time last season. The Lakers eventually ran out of plans for him, which is why they waived him before the season began to make room on the roster.

"The Los Angeles Lakers are waiving 2024 No. 17 pick Dalton Knecht, sources tell ESPN," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

Knecht became a highly sought-after free agent once he cleared waivers. After being one of the Lakers' best-kept secrets early in his career, he could become one of the team's biggest mistakes as time goes on. The former first-round pick ultimately decided to sign with the New York Knicks .

"Former Lakers forward Dalton Knecht has agreed to sign with the New York Knicks on a two-way NBA contract, his agents at Excel Sports Management tell ESPN," Charania wrote.

On Wednesday night, Knecht made his Knicks debut against the Chicago Bulls . The former Laker had a productive night off the bench, finishing with 10 points and seven rebounds. After the game, New York head coach Mike Brown made it clear that he views Knecht as a scorer, not just a shooter.

"He's a scorer. He's not just a shooter. A lot of people think he's a shooter because he's white. I said it for you. I hope I don't get in trouble," Brown told the media.

There is no doubt that Brown made his thoughts on Knecht clear. Defensively, Knecht may still struggle at times, but he looked closer to his former self on offense.

It was a great night for the Knicks all around, and Knecht took advantage of the opportunity in front of him. Brown clearly thinks highly of him as a scorer, so it will be interesting to see how Knecht's role evolves moving forward.

articles.title: Watch Travis Hunter's Mic'd Up Reaction to Seeing WWE Icon Big Show at Jaguars Game
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter couldn't help but be starstruck when WWE legend Big Show made an appearance at Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter couldn't help but be starstruck when WWE legend Big Show made an appearance at Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts.

Hunter was mic'd up when he had a fan moment on the sidelines as Big Show was introduced.

"The Big Show! That's tough! The Big Show! I know my brother up there going crazy," he said.

Hunter and the Jags went on to earn a 42-7 win over the Colts, and they will try to keep the momentum going when they face the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football .
